## 2026-05-07 — D-M1-CP5c-LAYER3-MODULE-AMENDED

**Decision:** Sub-session M1-CP5c (Layer 3 module + harness amended per ADR-007 Revisions 1–7) landed. All seven Revisions implemented in `/website/src/lib/translation-sandwich/layer3-prose.ts` and `/website/scripts/verify-translation-sandwich.ts`. Founder ran the harness locally with `LAYER1_REPLAY_CACHE=1 LAYER3_FORCE_REGEN=1`; first run surfaced two hard fails on F3 + F8 (single-snapshot disclaimer dropped despite temporal hooks — the Pattern B drift the founder anticipated at M1-CP5b open Q1). One in-session amendment landed: the Revision 5 single-snapshot section was strengthened with explicit MANDATORY language + comprehensive temporal-hook list including "I keep [verb-ing]" patterns + "err on the side of firing" instruction. Re-run produced 282/283 (the remaining failure was a one-off F4 JSON parse failure — Sonnet variance on output formatting, production-safe via the ADR-004 §9.3 catch path → `generateFallbackProse`). Founder fired four parallel-run rows via `/admin/test-reason` at standard depth (F1–F4). Per-row spot-check confirmed all seven Revisions pass: closing lines action-oriented (Revision 1); voice as guidance with proportional rebalance (Revisions 2 + 7); consistent Greek-to-English glossing on first occurrence per response (Revision 3); careful false-judgement framing applied (Revision 4); marginal-case sentences mid-prose with input-condition heuristic working as designed — F2 correctly OMITTED single-snapshot disclaimer (no temporal hook in "I should have spoken up at the meeting today"); F1 + F3 + F4 correctly INCLUDED disclaimer (hooks present); EUPATHEIA / praxis-motivation paths not exercised on the F1–F4 set (Revision 5); preferred-indifferent observations surfaced with the row 5b8bf957 shape rendered explicitly (Revision 6).

**Reasoning:** M1-CP5b adopted seven Revisions to ADR-007 with implementation deferred to M1-CP5c. ## 2026-05-07 — D-M1-CP5e-LAYER3-Q2-Q6-RESOLVED-2026-05-07

**Decision:** Append ADR-007 Amendment 3 (in-place sibling to Amendments 2026-05-07 from M1-CP5b + M1-CP5d; sixth recurrence of the in-place ADR amendment pattern, PR8 candidate held one more cycle per founder direction at session open) and apply mirroring module changes to `LAYER3_SYSTEM_PROMPT_API_REASON` + `generateProse`. Two scopes landed: (a) **Q2 — truncation defense + prompt strengthening (three concrete changes).** Q2 was investigated at session open; finding surfaced that the M1-CP5e prompt's framing of Q2 as "extractJSON does not currently strip [markdown fences]" was inaccurate — `extractJSON` already has a six-step fallback chain including markdown-fence stripping at Step 2 (`json-utils.ts` lines 28–37). The original F4 failure (`extractJSON: Could not extract valid JSON (2708 chars). Preview: ` ```json `` recorded in `D-M1-CP5c-LAYER3-MODULE-AMENDED-2026-05-07` Open Q2) was re-diagnosed as truncation at the LLM call (max_tokens cap), not parser limitation. Three concrete fixes: `max_tokens` default raised 2000 → 3000 in `generateProse`; explicit `stop_reason === 'max_tokens'` check added before `extractJSON` (throws diagnosable error instead of opaque parse failure six steps later); OUTPUT instruction tightened in §3 + closing instruction (first-character `{` / last-character `}` discipline; explicit "no markdown fences"; "no code-block syntax") as belt-and-braces. (b) **Q6 — STAGE DISCIPLINE rule.** New sub-section added to philosophical_reflection STRUCTURE (founder elected over COMPOSITION CONTRACT placement at session open) clarifying that prose names the stage where the passion is lodged (`passion_diagnosis.passions_detected[].causal_stage_affected`), not upstream stages, unless the assessment explicitly names them as part of the corrective sequence. Founder elected the three-fix Q2 scope ("All three this session") at investigation; Amendment 3 sibling option elected over absorb-into-Amendment-2.

**Reasoning:** Predecessor entry `D-M1-CP5d-LAYER3-AMENDMENT-2-2026-05-07` carried two open-question items into M1-CP5e (Q2 + Q6). Q2 investigation at session open changed the diagnosis. The session-prompt's Q2 framing assumed a parser gap (markdown fences not stripped); reading `json-utils.ts` showed Steps 1–6 in `extractJSON` (bare parse → fence-strip → regex first-`{`-to-last-`}` → index-based first-`{`-to-last-`}` → colon-repair → line-removal). The fence half of the F4 failure was already handled at Step 2. The malformed-JSON-internals half (diagnosed at M1-CP5c as "likely truncation or string-escape issue") was the load-bearing problem — extractJSON cannot repair a response truncated mid-string. The M1-CP5d-amended prompt is materially longer than the M1-CP5b version (3 OUTPUT examples + extended CONTROLLED VOCABULARY + extended COMPOSITION CONTRACT); responses approached the 2000-token cap. The fix moved from "prompt strengthening OR extractJSON extension" (the original session-prompt Q2 framing) to "raise max_tokens + diagnosable stop_reason check + tighten prompt as belt-and-braces" (the founder-elected Q2 scope after investigation). Q6 was resolved per the session-prompt direction with the founder's STRUCTURE-section placement preference. Both items are surface-level prose-quality / parse-discipline refinements that do not change the analytical engine (Layer 1 + Layer 2 unaffected). M1-CP6 cutover remains deferred until return-to-M1-CP5-prime.

This contradicts the assessment (a COMPOSITION CONTRACT violation, more serious than soft miss). **Decision:** Sub-session M1-CP5f landed Amendment 4 to ADR-007 + mirror module changes to `LAYER3_SYSTEM_PROMPT_API_REASON`. Two complementary fixes per founder direction at return-to-M1-CP5-prime: **D1 Option (b)** — additive fourth OUTPUT example demonstrating `direction_of_travel = stable` + iterative input + no marginal-case sentences firing (Pattern A — iterative phobos at synkatathesis, founder-elected at session-open over Pattern B); **D2 in** — defensive removal of M1-CP3's MANDATORY framing from §3 COMPOSITION CONTRACT marginal/undecidable bullets (three bullets) + §3 PROSE FIELDS philosophical_reflection bullets (two bullets), preserving Revision 5's input-condition heuristic which already covers all three marginal fields. Module bullet headers reframed from "**MANDATORY when condition + heuristic both fire**" to "**input-condition heuristic governs firing**" with added CRITICAL clause naming the assessment-side-mismatch case as a COMPOSITION CONTRACT violation (closing the n=5 hard miss directly). **Reasoning:** Per `D-RETURN-TO-M1-CP5-PRIME-RUBRIC-REFRESH-2026-05-07`, two surfaced items on Revision 5 (single-snapshot disclaimer) needed addressing before M1-CP6 cutover: a soft miss at n=4 (input-condition heuristic violated — input lacked iterative temporal hook but disclaimer fired anyway) and a hard miss at n=5 (disclaimer fired on `direction_of_travel = stable` — a COMPOSITION CONTRACT violation, prose contradicting assessment). Most likely root cause was structural: ADR-007 §3 PROSE FIELDS bullets retained M1-CP3's MANDATORY framing alongside Revision 5's input-condition heuristic; the two co-existed in the prompt and the LLM defaulted to the older MANDATORY pattern. Compounding this, two of three OUTPUT examples (Examples 1 + 2) carried the disclaimer; Example 3 (M1-CP5d) demonstrated omission for a horme case but the synkatathesis examples both fired the disclaimer, pattern-defaulting the LLM toward firing. This was the same shape as the Q1 OUTPUT-example over-imitation issue from M1-CP5d, migrated from causal-stage selection to marginal-case sentence firing. The complementary D1 + D2 scope addresses both reinforcing surfaces: D2 removes the residual MANDATORY signal so Revision 5's heuristic is the sole governing rule; D1 adds Example 4 (synkatathesis-lodged with stable trajectory, omission by design) so two of four examples now demonstrate omission and pattern-default toward firing is corrected. The CRITICAL clauses added to the bullet bodies (naming the assessment-side condition explicitly — "when direction_of_travel is anything other than 'single_snapshot'... OMIT this sentence regardless of input"; "when is_kathekon is true or false (not null), OMIT this sentence regardless of input") close the n=5 hard miss directly by naming the COMPOSITION CONTRACT semantics in line with the heuristic.

## 2026-05-08 — D-M1-CP6-CUTOVER-2026-05-08

**Decision:** Sub-session M1-CP6 — cutover commit applied. The bundled-depth call to `runSageReason` was removed from `/api/reason`; the translation-sandwich engine (`runSandwich` orchestrator over Layer 1 → Layer 2 → Layer 3) is now the sole user-facing path. Response shape changed from bundled-depth single object (`{ result, meta }`) to `translation-sandwich-v1` (`{ version, extraction, assessment, prose, meta, disclaimer }`) per ADR-004 §2.1. Cutover deployed to Vercel production; four verifications passed. **Layer 3 module status moves from Verified → Live; M1 arc completes.** R10 announcement declined under 3c election; founder accepted the trade-off explicitly. Three design choices elected at session-open: 1C (deterministic minimal fallback for Layer 1/2 throws — no bundled fallback), 2A (parallel-run retired — `runParallelSandwich` deprecated, retained for offline/testing), 3A (Tier 1 force-clarification first-turn surfacing wired via `issueContinuationToken`).

**Reasoning:** Per ADR-004 §10's checkpoint table, M1-CP6 is the cutover commit row — Critical-tier deployment-config change activating new prose path on the user-facing route. Predecessor session (RTM1-CP5-prime-prime, `D-RETURN-TO-M1-CP5-PRIME-PRIME-RUBRIC-REFRESH-2026-05-08`) verified 39/40 prose micro-checks, closed the hard miss, accepted F4 soft miss as known limitation post-cutover, and authorised cutover via founder's Branch A election. This session executed the cutover under the full Critical Change Protocol per project instructions §0c-ii. Founder elected 3c (skip R10 announcement) on grounds that no external `/api/reason` consumers are known despite agent_card.json + llms.txt agent discovery surface — the trade-off was named, founder owns the call. Three design choices (1C + 2A + 3A) elected after AI surfaced architectural ambiguity in ADR-004 (§9.1 vs §10 CP6 reconciliation), parallel-run posture options (2.A vs 2.B), and Tier 1 surfacing scope (3A vs 3B). Founder also surfaced and deferred a 2F architectural arc — captured in §"Deferred decision" below per PR7. Diff applied: 2 files touched (~150 LOC net change); both files edited via Edit tool with founder reading the diff in chat before approval. Critical Change Protocol's six steps captured visibly in the conversation; founder approved with "approved" — explicit acknowledgment of the four named risks (R10 / external-consumer breaking change; R20a perimeter preservation; Layer 1 failure visibility change under 1C; TRANSLATION_SANDWICH_TIER1_SECRET env-var dependency for 3A).

**Critical Change Protocol record (per project instructions §0c-ii — six steps verbatim from session conversation):**

1. **What is changing — plain language.** /api/reason stops calling the bundled-depth engine entirely. It now calls only the translation-sandwich engine and returns the sandwich's response. From the user's point of view: when they hit /api/reason, they receive a response with a different structure — fields named `extraction`, `assessment`, and `prose` (each carrying the explicit Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3 outputs) instead of the bundled-depth single object. The bundled engine code remains in `/website/src/lib/sage-reason-engine.ts` for other endpoints (M2/M3/M4 consumer migrations). Three new behaviors come with the cutover: Tier 1 force-clarification responses now reach the user (with a continuation token to re-submit after answering), Layer 1/2 failures return a polite minimal-shape fallback (no bundled call, no error to the user), and the response always carries the R3 disclaimer.

2. **What could break — specific worst case.** Four named risks: (a) external agent developers parsing /api/reason responses against the bundled-depth shape will see breaking change at cutover — their parsers fail on the new shape; per 3c election, no R10 announcement; if external consumers exist (the agent_card.json + llms.txt agent discovery surface implies some may), they get no warning. (b) The R20a perimeter at line 173 must remain inviolate (AC5 + PR6); the diff preserves it verbatim with `runSandwich` strictly AFTER `enforceDistressCheck`. (c) Layer 1 LLM failures during cutover — today silently absorbed by bundled fallback; post-cutover under 1C user sees a polite minimal-shape fallback (200 status, structured response with `fallback: true` in meta); behavior change, honest, not stranding the user, but visibly different. (d) TRANSLATION_SANDWICH_TIER1_SECRET env var must be set on Vercel for Tier 1 issuance to work; if unset and Tier 1 fires, user sees 503 with `continuation_token_engine_unavailable`; per predecessor production state, env var is already set in all three environments.

3. **What happens to existing sessions.** Auth/session unaffected. The cutover does not touch authentication, session cookies, JWT validation, or session-bridge state. The translation-sandwich path sits POST-perimeter (per ADR-004 §8); existing user sessions continue uninterrupted. On their next /api/reason call they receive the new response shape, but the session itself is preserved. AC7 NOT engaged.

4. **Rollback plan.** `git revert HEAD` of the cutover commit + `git push origin main`. Vercel rebuild restores the parallel-run flow as user-facing. Rollback is itself a breaking change going the other way for any external consumers who adopted the new schema during the cutover window — public "rollback in effect" notice required if rollback occurs even though no R10 announcement was made before cutover.

5. **Verification step (founder-performable, post-deploy).** Four verifications named: (1) Happy path, new shape — non-distressing fixture via /admin/test-reason; confirm version + extraction + assessment + prose + disclaimer present; NOT bundled-depth shape. (2) R20a perimeter still fires — distress-flagged input ("I've been thinking about ending my life..."); confirm `{ distress_detected: true, severity, redirect_message }`; engine NOT called. (3) Tier 1 surfacing — fixture F7 (ELEMENT_FUSION); confirm `clarification_required: true`, `intake_tier: 1`, non-empty `continuation_token`. (4) Vercel logs clean — no `[/api/reason]` errors around deploy timestamp.

6. **Explicit founder approval specific to named risks.** Founder responded "approved" — having read the four named risks in Step 2 (especially the R10 / external-consumer risk under 3c, and the Layer 1 failure visibility change under 1C). Approval was for THIS commit only, not blanket M1-arc approval.

**Deferred decision (per PR7 — Decisions Not Made Are Documented) — 2F architectural arc:**

**What was considered:** Founder proposed 2F at M1-CP6 session-open as an alternative to 2A/2B/2C parallel-run posture options. The proposal: after sandwich Layer 2 lands, surface three components — (A) numerical scores per Layer 2 step + final outcome (for agents, UI graphics, longitudinal proximity tracking); (B) current Sonnet Layer 3 prose (unchanged); (C) new Opus 4.7 LLM call taking raw input + raw user data + Layer 2 path/output, producing input-specific contextualizing prose in an integrative voice. Bundled engine repurposed as testing/curiosity-only path (which 2A retirement effectively achieves).

**Founder's underlying intent:** preserve bundled's input-specific responsiveness — the value bundled offers that sandwich Layer 3 (Sonnet) doesn't fully capture — by replacing bundled with a more capable LLM (Opus) that has explicit access to both the raw input AND the deterministic Layer 2 assessment. The deterministic Layer 2 stays stable (auditable, reviewable); a more capable LLM produces the input-specific responsive prose on top.

**Why deferred:** (a) 2F is a substantial architectural change — not a parallel-run posture decision but an engine-architecture change adding a new layer (Layer 4 or Layer 3b). (b) Larger than M1-CP6 was scoped for — would require multiple ADRs, cost projection work, parallel-run observation of the new Opus layer before user-facing ship. (c) Per PR1 single-endpoint discipline + ADR-004 §10 parallel-run-before-cutover pattern, 2F should be its own multi-session arc with parallel-run observation before cutover. (d) Shipping 2F today would have been the first time this project commits an LLM-layer architecture without observation data first.

**Four open clarifying questions (founder to answer at 2F arc session-open):**

(i) **Model.** "Opus 4.7" — AI's system prompt model list as of May 2026 names Claude Opus 4.6 as latest Opus. Founder to confirm: is 4.7 actually shipped, or is "4.7" shorthand for "the latest Opus available"?

(ii) **Replace or augment Layer 3?** Three sub-options: (1) Opus replaces Sonnet Layer 3 entirely — single prose output. (2) Opus runs alongside Sonnet Layer 3 — user sees both. (3) Layer 3 retired in favor of Opus producing both structured fields AND integrative voice.

(iii) **Component A — numerical scoring scope.** Per-mechanism quality scores (already exist as qualitative `assessment.stage_scores`)? Final proximity score? Both? Categorical-as-numeric (1–5 mapping to existing 5 levels) or true numeric (0–100)? Affects R6c reconciliation — R6c says "Qualitative proximity levels, not numeric 0–100" so true-numeric requires R6c amendment (Critical-tier governance change).

(iv) **Component C — "other raw text data stored from the user."** What's in scope? Practitioner_context + project_context (current four-layer)? Mentor profile? Journal entries? Recent interaction history? All of the above?

**Cost + latency considerations to surface at 2F arc session-open:**

- Per-request cost roughly tripling: current sandwich ~$0.034 → with Opus added ~$0.10–0.13. R5 ratio (paid-tier revenue must cover ≥2x LLM cost) compresses meaningfully. Deliberate-choice exercise per R0 + R5 needed.
- Latency: Opus calls run ~25–40s for prompts of this complexity; current Sonnet L3 ~17s. Sequential = 50–70s, near Vercel 60s timeout. Parallel Opus + Sonnet (max 25–40s) recommended over sequential.

**Governance work 2F arc would trigger:**

- ADR-009 (or ADR-004 amendment) — new Layer 4 / Layer 3b specification.
- AC1 amendment — add Opus row to model selection table.
- R6c reconciliation — depending on Component A scoring scope.
- R5 cost projection update.
- ADR-007 amendment or supersession — depending on whether Sonnet Layer 3 is retired.
- Verification harness extension — Opus output validation, R7 source fidelity, R8a/R8c discipline.
- New module: `layer4-opus-contextualization.ts` (or `layer3b-opus.ts`).

**Sequencing recommendation:** treat 2F as a separate architectural arc — call it "M1-Plus" or "Layer 3b Opus contextualization arc." Parallel-run observation of the Opus layer before user-facing ship.

## 2026-05-09 — D-ITEM-I-viii-CONSUMER-PAGE-ADAPTATION-2026-05-09

**Decision:** Sub-session Item I (viii) — consumer-page-vs-API-shape adaptation following the M1-CP6 cutover (2026-05-08). Four reasoning-display surfaces adapted to the translation-sandwich-v1 response shape: (1) /mentor-hub mentor-reply path now reads `data.prose.philosophical_reflection` with safe fallbacks (was reading `data.result || data.response` and falling through to "I acknowledge your message." placeholder every turn); (2) /ops-hub Stoic Check display shows a structured prose.philosophical_reflection + improvement_guidance + summary three-paragraph layout plus qualitative `assessment.katorthoma_proximity` per R6c (was reading `reasoning` + numeric `proximity_rating`, falling through to JSON dump); (3) /ops-hub Alert evaluation display does minimum-extraction reading `prose.summary` with `philosophical_reflection` fallback (was reading `reasoning`, falling through to JSON dump); (4) /ops-hub Decision Scoring display polished per founder election — ranked option cards with proximity badge + kathekon line + stoic_insight paragraph + passions_detected chips, recommended option highlighted with green border + star, reasoning_receipt summary, disclaimer (was reading `comparison` + `recommendation`, falling through to JSON dump). All four surfaces additionally handle distress-detected (`{distress_detected: true, redirect_message}`) and Tier-1 force-clarification (`{clarification_required: true, clarification: {question_text}}`) auxiliary shapes explicitly. /private-mentor audited; no adaptation needed (the page's /api/reason call awaits-and-discards). Item I bundle: (i)+(ii)+(iii)+(vi)+(vii)+(viii) Closed; (iv)+(v) remain open.

**Reasoning:** Direct continuation of the post-M1-CP6 hygiene cleanup. The translation-sandwich-v1 cutover replaced the bundled-engine response shape on /api/reason with `{version, extraction, assessment, prose, meta, disclaimer}`; consumer pages still read the old `data.result || data.response` / `data.reasoning` / `data.comparison` fields. Pre-fix user impact: real reasoning prose was hidden behind placeholder text on /mentor-hub and behind raw JSON on /ops-hub for every reasoning-display surface. Founder-elected scope: bundle all four surfaces in one session (vs split); presentable polish on Decision Scoring; minimum extraction on the other three. The polish elaboration is justified by Decision Scoring being the highest-information-density surface (per-option ranking + structured fields + receipts) and the only surface where minimum extraction would still produce a hard-to-read display (multiple option records concatenated). Per /api/score-decision route handler reading, the buildEnvelope shape places the meaningful fields at `result.options_scored[]`, `result.recommended`, `result.reasoning_receipt`, `result.disclaimer`. Per /lib/translation-sandwich/parallel-run.ts (`runSandwich` happy-path return) and /lib/translation-sandwich/layer3-prose.ts (`Layer3Prose` interface), the user-facing prose fields on /api/reason are `prose.philosophical_reflection`, `prose.improvement_guidance`, `prose.summary`. The minimal-fallback shape (route lines 363-389) shares the same prose field names, so the adaptations work transparently across happy-path + minimal-fallback responses.

## 2026-05-10 — D-A1-LAYER2-AUTH-SCAFFOLD-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A1 (Layer 2 server-side authentication infrastructure for plugin-originated calls) is scaffolded on `/api/reason` as the PR1 single-endpoint proof. A new function `checkPluginAuth` is added to `/website/src/app/api/reason/route.ts` that reads an `X-Plugin-Auth` HTTP header, performs a constant-time comparison against the `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET` environment variable using node:crypto's `timingSafeEqual`, and returns `{valid: true, plugin_id: string}` on match or `{valid: false, error: NextResponse}` on any failure. A feature flag `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` is added (currently set to `'false'`) governing whether the function is allowed to run. **The function is defined but NOT INVOKED in this session** — the scaffold exists in the code with zero runtime effect; the eventual invocation site lands in a subsequent session after the Critical Change Protocol's deploy-phase review. A new `/website/.env.example` file is created documenting `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` (default `false`) and `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET` (placeholder; real value in `/website/.env.local` and Vercel project settings, never committed). Companion ADR `/adopted/ADR-stoic-agent-substrate-concept.md` (Stage 1 item J1) is adopted under this entry, capturing the three-layer substrate architecture, three-layer R20a defence, two-front-ends-one-substrate pattern, moat boundary, and consequences.

**Critical Change Protocol writeup (six steps, full form, per project instructions §0c-ii and standing-cache §"Critical-risk sessions"):**

1. **What is changing** — A new authentication-check function (`checkPluginAuth`) and a feature flag (`PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED`, default `false`) are added to `/website/src/app/api/reason/route.ts`. The function reads the `X-Plugin-Auth` header, performs a constant-time comparison against `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET`, and returns a structured pass/fail result. The function is defined but not invoked — the scaffold exists with zero runtime effect. A new `/website/.env.example` file documents the flag and the companion secret placeholder. The existing user-auth + API-key dual-auth pattern is unchanged. PR1 single-endpoint proof discipline: scaffolded only on `/api/reason`; no other route files touched.

2. **What could break** — Worst case: if the function is invoked (flag flipped to `true`) and `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET` is missing or malformed, plugin-originated requests would receive 401 responses while user-auth and API-key requests continue working. This is the intended fail-closed behaviour for plugin auth, but it would block legitimate plugin traffic until the secret is set. **In this session, the flag stays at `false` and the function is not invoked, so this failure mode cannot fire.** If a future bug introduced a code path that called `checkPluginAuth` regardless of the flag, the worst case would still be limited to plugin-originated traffic; existing user-auth and API-key paths remain unaffected because `checkPluginAuth` does not modify or short-circuit them.

3. **What happens to existing sessions** — N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate. Per the no-current-users governing note added to the build-arc cache in this session (logged via `D-BUILD-CACHE-DRIFT-RESOLVED-2026-05-10-NO-USERS`).

4. **Rollback plan** — Three rollback paths in order of decreasing scope. (a) **No-deploy rollback (this session's posture):** the scaffold commit is not deployed. Rollback is simply not deploying. The flag remains `false` even if deployed; rollback is "leave the flag off." (b) **Flag-off rollback (if deployed):** ensure `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` is not set in Vercel environment variables, or set it to `false`. The function exists in code but is never invoked. Effectively a no-op deploy. (c) **Code-revert rollback:** `git revert <scaffold-commit-hash>` and `git push origin main`. Vercel redeploys the prior route handler. This is the strongest rollback path.

5. **Verification step** — In-session (no deploy): two grep commands confirm scaffold presence and zero call sites. Expected: function defined at line ~199; flag declaration at line ~170; zero call sites of `checkPluginAuth(...)` other than the function declaration itself; `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=false` declared in `/website/.env.example`. Post-deploy verification (next session, after deploy + flag-flip): a `curl` test of `/api/reason` with and without the `X-Plugin-Auth` header against the real `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET` value, confirming 200 with valid secret and 401 without when the flag is on; confirming all paths still return 200 (with user-auth or API-key) when the flag is off.

6. **Explicit founder approval** — Requested for the scaffold commit only, NOT for deploy. The deploy approval is a separate explicit-approval moment in the next session after CCP review of any post-scaffold-discovered risks (per PR1 single-endpoint proof discipline — verify on `/api/reason` before any rollout). The founder responds "go ahead" specific to the named risks above (or pushes back) before staging the scaffold commit.

Existing route handler unchanged. No call sites added.
- `/website/.env.example` — created with `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=false` declaration, `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET=` placeholder, header documenting convention, and per-variable inline rationale referencing the ADR and staging plan.
- `/adopted/ADR-stoic-agent-substrate-concept.md` — created (companion ADR for Stage 1 item J1; captures three-layer architecture, three-layer R20a defence, two-front-ends-one-substrate, moat boundary, consequences).
- `/operations/decision-log.md` — this entry appended.

## 2026-05-10 — D-A1-INVOCATION-SITE-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A1 (Layer 2 server-side authentication infrastructure for plugin-originated calls) reaches **Wired** status on `/api/reason`. The `checkPluginAuth` function scaffolded under `D-A1-LAYER2-AUTH-SCAFFOLD-2026-05-10` is now actually invoked from the POST handler's authentication branch. Founder elected **Option (a) — extend the existing 401 branch** from the three options named in the scaffold-predecessor entry's Open Question 1. The other two options ((b) third precedence tier checked first; (c) pre-handler middleware refactor) are deferred to post-A2 dedicated sessions and are not foreclosed by this decision. Commit `6e57663` ("Stage 1 A1 invocation site: extend 401 branch with plugin-auth (Option a)") landed on origin/main and Vercel deployed it cleanly. Companion entry `D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10` (next entry) records the deploy + flag-flip + three verification scenarios.

**Reasoning for Option (a):** Lowest blast radius (the only branch touched is the one that already fails authentication today); strongest PR1 single-endpoint proof discipline (minimum new code surface; minimum risk that today's regression smoke test would not catch a flaw); fits the 4-hour Critical-tier session budget cleanly; preserves Options (b) and (c) on the table for later sessions when the substrate's needs are better understood. Acknowledged limitations of (a): plugin-auth is checked *last*, after both user-auth and API-key have failed (a request carrying both a valid Supabase JWT and an `X-Plugin-Auth` header is treated as a user-auth call and never reaches plugin-auth); and the option is unlikely to be the long-term shape once A2/A3/A4 land and migration tiers begin calling Layer 2. Acceptable per PR1 — prove the auth path on one endpoint first, refactor later. Recommendation aligned with founder election.

**Critical Change Protocol writeup (six steps, full form, per project instructions §0c-ii and standing-cache §"Critical-risk sessions"):**

1. **What is changing** — Inside `/website/src/app/api/reason/route.ts`, the existing branch that today returns `auth.error` (a 401 "Authentication required") whenever both user-auth and API-key checks have failed is extended to first try `checkPluginAuth(request)` if `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` is `true`. If plugin-auth succeeds, the request is treated as authenticated (with no `auth.user` — exactly like API-key callers, so `practitionerContext` resolves to `null`). If plugin-auth fails, its 401 response is returned in preference to the user-auth 401. If `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` is `false` (the post-deploy / pre-flag-flip production state), the new conditional short-circuits and behaviour is byte-identical to the prior scaffold state. Existing user-auth and API-key branches are not re-routed, re-ordered, or re-evaluated. The `void checkPluginAuth` scaffold-presence reference is removed (the function now has a real call site so tree-shaking is not a risk); the `void PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` reference is retained for symmetry. Doc-comments at the top of the A1 block and on the function are updated to reflect Wired status. PR1 single-endpoint discipline: scaffolded only on `/api/reason`; no other route file touched.

2. **What could break** — Three failure modes. (i) The 401-branch refactor accidentally breaks the existing branch (mis-shaped conditional returning `null` or skipping the existing return path). Mitigation: the new code preserves the *exact* current return path (`return auth.error`) as the default unless plugin-auth explicitly succeeds; verified by Scenario 3 in companion entry. (ii) Tree-shaking removes the function in production builds with `void checkPluginAuth` removed. Mitigation: the new call site references `checkPluginAuth` directly; Vercel build's TypeScript compilation would catch any unused-import error before deploy; verified by clean Vercel deploy (commit `6e57663`). (iii) CORS headers on the new 401 path differ from the existing 401 path (the existing `requireAuth` 401 does not set CORS headers; the new `checkPluginAuth` 401s do). Asymmetry intentional in the scaffold; flagged for transparency; for server-side plugin calls (the intended use), CORS is irrelevant.

3. **What happens to existing sessions** — N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate. Per the no-current-users governing note added to the build-arc cache under `D-BUILD-CACHE-DRIFT-RESOLVED-2026-05-10-NO-USERS`. The founder's own browser session on `sagereasoning.com` is *not* affected because user-auth runs first and continues to work exactly as before (verified by Scenario 3 in companion entry).

4. **Rollback plan** — `git revert 6e57663` and push via GitHub Desktop. Vercel auto-redeploys the prior code (the scaffold present, no invocation site, no third precedence tier). Rollback time: ≤5 minutes after Vercel finishes redeploying. Companion flag-off rollback (set `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=false` in Vercel) covers most flag-on issues without requiring code changes; recorded under companion entry `D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10`.

5. **Verification step** — Pre-deploy: in-session diff review of `/website/src/app/api/reason/route.ts`; founder confirmed the change matched the CCP-writeup description before approval. TypeScript compile check via `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` from the website root returned exit 0 with no errors. Function call-site count after the change: one declaration (line 204), one type reference `ReturnType<typeof checkPluginAuth>` (line 314), one real call site (line 321). Post-deploy with flag-off (Smoke Test 1 in sub-step 3 of the deploy sequence): founder ran a Stoic Check on /ops-hub at https://sagereasoning.com — got the standard three-paragraph translation-sandwich-v1 response; regression-clear; safe to flip flag. Post-deploy with flag-on: see three verification scenarios in companion entry.

6. **Explicit founder approval** — Requested specific to the three named risks above; founder responded "Go ahead" via AskUserQuestion before the code change was made.

## 2026-05-10 — D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A1 (Layer 2 server-side authentication infrastructure for plugin-originated calls) reaches **Verified** status on `/api/reason`. The PR1 single-endpoint proof is complete. Sequence: founder added `PLUGIN_AUTH_SECRET` to Vercel Production environment variables (a 64-character hex string generated via `openssl rand -hex 32`); founder mirrored the same value to `/website/.env.local` for local-dev parity (gitignored); founder committed and pushed the invocation-site change (commit `6e57663`); Vercel auto-deployed the new code cleanly; founder ran Smoke Test 1 (regression check with flag still off) — passed; founder added `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true` to Vercel Production environment variables; founder triggered a Vercel redeploy with cache disabled to ensure the new env var was picked up; redeploy went green; founder ran the three verification scenarios — all three passed. The build arc unblocks A2 (Layer 2 input validation surface scaffolding) for the next session.

**Reasoning:** This entry records the deploy + flag-flip as a separate Critical change from the invocation-site code change (companion entry `D-A1-INVOCATION-SITE-2026-05-10`). Per Critical Change Protocol discipline, the deploy + env-var-activation is itself a deployment-configuration change that activates a new auth surface in production — which is Critical regardless of how cleanly the code change deployed. Per PR1 single-endpoint proof discipline, A1 only reaches Verified after all three verification scenarios pass on the proof endpoint; the staging plan's Stage 1 success criteria for A1 require this status before A2 can begin. Per the staging plan's Session 2 packaging, A1 reaching Verified ends one session and unblocks the next (A2 Elevated risk per Session 3 packaging).

**Critical Change Protocol writeup (six steps, full form, per project instructions §0c-ii and standing-cache §"Critical-risk sessions"):**

1. **What is changing** — Two production-affecting changes in sequence. (i) Deploy the invocation-site code change: founder committed `website/src/app/api/reason/route.ts` (commit `6e57663`) and pushed via GitHub Desktop; Vercel auto-deployed; with `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` still unset (effectively `false`), the new conditional short-circuits and `checkPluginAuth` is never invoked at runtime; production behaviour byte-identical to pre-deploy. (ii) Flip the flag: founder added `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED=true` to Vercel Production env vars; triggered a redeploy with cache disabled; with the flag on, the conditional opens and `checkPluginAuth` runs whenever both user-auth and API-key have failed; plugin-originated requests with valid `X-Plugin-Auth` header now succeed; plugin-originated requests with missing/invalid header still get 401 (from `checkPluginAuth` instead of `requireAuth`); existing user-auth and API-key paths unchanged. Between (i) and (ii), founder ran Smoke Test 1 (regression check with flag off) and confirmed identical-to-pre-deploy behaviour before approving the flag-flip.

2. **What could break** — Three failure modes. (i) Vercel build fails on the invocation-site commit. Mitigation: TypeScript already compiled cleanly in sandbox; Vercel deploy went green. (ii) Flag-off regression — the new conditional somehow breaks existing user-auth or API-key path. Mitigation: Smoke Test 1 was the dedicated check for this; passed. (iii) Flag-on misbehaviour — three sub-cases verified by the three scenarios in step 5. None observed.

3. **What happens to existing sessions** — N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate. Per the no-current-users governing note added to the build-arc cache under `D-BUILD-CACHE-DRIFT-RESOLVED-2026-05-10-NO-USERS`. Founder's own browser session on `sagereasoning.com` confirmed unaffected by Smoke Test 1 (with flag off) and Scenario 3 (with flag on).

4. **Rollback plan** — Three paths, ordered by severity. (a) Flag-off rollback (covers most flag-on issues): in Vercel dashboard → sagereasoning project → Settings → Environment Variables → find `PLUGIN_AUTH_ENABLED` → either edit and change to `false`, or delete the variable entirely; save; Vercel redeploys; rollback time ≤5 min. The code remains live; only the flag toggle reverts. (b) Code-revert rollback (covers deploy failures or unexplained flag-off regressions): `git revert 6e57663` and push via GitHub Desktop; Vercel redeploys the prior code (scaffold present, no invocation site); rollback time ≤5 min. (c) Combined catastrophic rollback: both in sequence; the site returns to today's exact pre-deploy production state.

5. **Verification step (the three scenarios — all passed):**
   - **Scenario 1 — Valid plugin-auth returns 200.** `curl -X POST https://www.sagereasoning.com/api/reason -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Plugin-Auth: <real-secret>" -d '{"input":"...","depth":"quick"}'` — returned 200 with the standard `{"version":"translation-sandwich-v1","extraction":{...},"prose":{"philosophical_reflection":"...","improvement_guidance":"...","summary":"..."},"disclaimer":"..."}` shape. The first attempt against `https://sagereasoning.com` (no `www.`) returned a 15-byte "Redirecting..." response because Vercel redirects the apex domain to the canonical `www.` form and POST bodies do not survive the redirect; the re-run against the canonical `https://www.sagereasoning.com` succeeded. **Result: PASS.**
   - **Scenario 2 — Invalid plugin-auth returns 401.** Same curl with `X-Plugin-Auth: WRONG-SECRET-VALUE-FOR-TESTING-PURPOSES-ONLY-NOT-REAL` — returned 401 with `{"error":"Plugin authentication failed"}` from `checkPluginAuth` (not from `requireAuth`'s `"Authentication required. Please sign in."`), confirming the precedence preference in the new conditional correctly returns the plugin-auth error when plugin-auth was attempted. **Result: PASS.**
   - **Scenario 3 — Existing user-auth still returns 200 (zero regression).** Founder ran a Stoic Check on /ops-hub at https://sagereasoning.com (signed in) — got the standard three-paragraph translation-sandwich-v1 response. Identical behaviour to Smoke Test 1. Confirms flag-on did not disturb the existing user-auth path because user-auth runs first and succeeds before the new plugin-auth conditional is reached. **Result: PASS.**

## 2026-05-10 — D-A2-INPUT-VALIDATION-SURFACE-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A2 (Layer 2 input validation surface for plugin-originated calls) reaches **Verified** status on `/api/reason`. Plugin-authenticated callers per the substrate ADR submit a pre-computed `Layer1Schema` (the plugin ran Layer 1 locally) alongside the original input text. The route validates the schema via `validateLayer1Schema`, skips server-side `extractFeatures` + `loadLayer1WithFallback` (RAG retrieval), and feeds the validated schema directly to Layer 2 via `runSandwich`. R20a continues to run on the input text per AC5. Three design choices elected: **1(i)** new `Layer1Schema` ingress; **2(a)** R20a on original text alongside the schema; **3(β)** wrap `validateLayer1Schema` in a route-ingress helper (`validatePluginRequest`). All three were the recommended options. Three production verification scenarios passed: valid schema → 200 with `extraction` field returning the supplied schema; invalid schema (wrong `version` value) → 400 with `category` + `field` + `detail` preserved from `Layer1ValidationError`; existing user-auth path → 200 (zero regression). PR1 single-endpoint proof on `/api/reason` is COMPLETE for A2.

**Reasoning:** Choice 1(i) matches the substrate ADR (Decision §"The three layers") and sets up A3 (signing) cleanly — the schema is the thing to be cryptographically signed. Choice 2(a) preserves AC5 unchanged with no architectural commitment about the three-layer R20a defence's specific handover mechanism (which belongs in A7 and B2, not A2). Choice 3(β) mirrors the existing `requireAuth`/`validateApiKey` helper pattern in `security.ts` and converts `Layer1ValidationError` throws into structured 400 responses with the validator's `category` and `field` info preserved. Cross-references predecessor entries `D-A1-LAYER2-AUTH-SCAFFOLD-2026-05-10`, `D-A1-INVOCATION-SITE-2026-05-10`, `D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10`.

## 2026-05-10 — D-A3-LAYER2-SIGNING-ADR-ADOPTED-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A3 (Layer 2 signing infrastructure) ADR drafted, founder-approved, and moved to `/adopted/ADR-layer2-signing-infrastructure.md` (Path A elected at session-open). Four named design choices committed to architecture: **(1) Ed25519** asymmetric signing via `node:crypto` native primitives (rejected HMAC, ECDSA P-256, hybrid); **(2) `Layer2Assessment` only** as the signed payload with canonical-JSON serialisation (rejected composed sandwich output, `Layer1Schema + Layer2Assessment` together, hash-of-canonical-JSON); **(3) hybrid distribution** of the public verification key via both a new `/api/public-key` endpoint and the plugin manifest's `signing_keys` block (rejected API-discovery-only, manifest-only, HMAC-secret-via-plugin-auth); **(4) single key with quarterly rotation and 30-day overlap window** (rejected long-lived no-rotation, key-per-Layer-2-version, defer-to-separate-ADR). Wire format becomes `{assessment, signature, key_id}` in place of bare `Layer2Assessment` in the composed sandwich output. A3 implementation status: **Scoped → Designed**. Decision status: **Adopted**.

**Reasoning:** Ed25519 + asymmetric is the architecturally honest choice for a substrate whose value proposition includes third-party verifiability — verifiers need only the public key, never the signing capability. `Layer2Assessment` only is the smallest moat-aligned payload per the substrate ADR's §"The moat boundary" — signing makes Layer 2 authoritative without entangling the signing surface with Layer 3's intentional per-consumer prose adaptation per `prose_mode`. Hybrid distribution combines plugin-manifest offline verification (works without network; manifest is the trust anchor against MITM on key fetch) with API-discovery rotation support (rotation can publish a new key without forcing immediate plugin updates). Single-key quarterly rotation with 30-day overlap matches the founder's operational scale (one signer; manual rotation cadence sustainable) while building rotation hygiene before any compromise event makes it urgent. Cross-references predecessor entries `D-A2-INPUT-VALIDATION-SURFACE-2026-05-10` (the validated input contract A3 will sign), `D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10` (A1 plugin-auth ingress this signing surface is reachable from), `D-STAGING-PLAN-ADOPTED-2026-05-10` (Stage 1 A3 commitment), and the substrate ADR `/adopted/ADR-stoic-agent-substrate-concept.md` §"The moat boundary" (the architectural anchor for why signing matters here).

## 2026-05-10 — D-A3-LAYER2-SIGNING-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-10

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A3 (Layer 2 signing infrastructure) reaches **Verified** status on `/api/reason`. The substrate now signs every authoritative `Layer2Assessment` with an Ed25519 signature when `SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_SIGNING_ENABLED='true'`; verifiers (plugins, downstream agents, third-party auditors) check signatures against the public key published at `/api/public-key`. Three session-opening elections committed: **Choice 1(a)** wire-format change is feature-flag-gated via `SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_SIGNING_ENABLED` so Path A rollback is "flip flag false" (~30s recovery via Vercel redeploy); **Choice 2(a)** canonical-JSON serialisation is implemented in-house in `layer2-canonical-json.ts` with deterministic key ordering, `NaN`/`Infinity`/`undefined` rejection, and `-0` normalisation; **Choice 3(a)** `/api/public-key` endpoint serves the verification key with no authentication and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=3600` edge caching. Three production verification scenarios passed: **Scenario 1** (`SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_SIGNING_ENABLED='false'`) returned a bare `Layer2Assessment` shape with `assessment.version='layer2-assessment-v1'` and no `signature`/`key_id` fields — zero regression confirmed; **Scenario 2** (flag flipped to `'true'` + Vercel redeployed) returned the wrapped `{assessment, signature, key_id}` shape; the 88-character base64 Ed25519 signature verified against the public key fetched from `/api/public-key` (key_id `substrate-layer2-2026Q2`); **Scenario 3** mutated `ruling_faculty_state` to `'TAMPERED'` and re-canonicalised — the signature correctly failed verification, confirming the perturbation discipline at the production boundary. PR1 single-endpoint proof on `/api/reason` is COMPLETE for A3. A3 implementation status: **Designed → Scaffolded → Wired → Verified** (all four transitions in this session). The build arc proceeds to A4 — Key management.

**Reasoning:** The ADR's four design choices (Ed25519 asymmetric signing; `Layer2Assessment` only as the signed payload; hybrid public-key distribution via API discovery + plugin manifest; single key with quarterly rotation and 30-day overlap window) translated cleanly into implementation. Choice 1(a) feature-flag-gated rollout was elected over hard cutover and versioned response shape because it gives the substrate a sub-30-second rollback path (the most important property when the codebase has no current users beyond the founder + test logins per the build-arc cache governing note, and the next user-base extension is an unknown distance away). Choice 2(a) in-house canonical-JSON was elected over a third-party library (json-canon, RFC 8785 implementation) because the helper is small (~135 lines including doc-comments), bound to the `Layer2Assessment` type shape, and avoids adding a new dependency to the audit surface — the codebase's dependency-minimisation preference. Choice 3(a) edge-cached unauthenticated `/api/public-key` was elected over rate-limited or no-cache because the verification key is, by definition, public; aggressive edge caching is the right operational posture; rate-limiting infrastructure is unnecessary complexity for a public read. Cross-references predecessor entries `D-A3-LAYER2-SIGNING-ADR-ADOPTED-2026-05-10` (the architectural anchor; four design choices committed), `D-A2-INPUT-VALIDATION-SURFACE-2026-05-10` (the validated input contract this signing surface signs), `D-A1-FLAG-FLIP-VERIFIED-2026-05-10` (the plugin-auth ingress this signing surface is reachable from).

Single export `canonicaliseLayer2Assessment(assessment): string`. Sorts object keys lexicographically at every nesting level via `Object.keys(...).sort()` (UTF-16 code-unit comparison; matches RFC 8785 §3.2.3 ordering for the all-ASCII Layer2Assessment field set). Arrays preserve order. Strings via `JSON.stringify` (handles escapes, controls, surrogates per ECMA-404). Single export `signLayer2Assessment(assessment): SignedLayer2Assessment` returning `{ assessment, signature, key_id }`. Reads `SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_SIGNING_KEY` (PEM PKCS#8 private key) and `SUBSTRATE_LAYER2_KEY_ID` at call time per the `tier1-token.ts` discipline. ## 2026-05-12 — D-A5-LAYER3-SCAFFOLDED-VERIFIED-2026-05-12

**Decision:** Stage 1 item A5 (Layer 3 server-side substrate service) reaches **Scaffolded + Wired + Verified** status on the `/api/reason` PR1 single-endpoint proof. A new substrate library module `/website/src/lib/substrate/layer3-service.ts` (~600 lines) exposes two entry points (`applyLayer3Injections` — minimum-disruption wrapper used by existing consumers; `generateLayer3Response` — full service for future plugin-originated consumers) plus six deterministic injection helpers (R3 evaluative disclaimer; R19c limitations link; R19d mirror principle; R20a distress pass-through; R18a Character Kernel category language; R18e Article 50 transparency notice placeholder) plus three forward-looking type families (Layer2Decision four-outcome envelope per AC9; Provenance + UsePolicy tags per AC10; OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-conventions span stub per AC11). A new public-API route `/website/src/app/api/substrate/layer3/route.ts` (~125 lines) returns 503 when the flag is OFF; ready for plugin-originated traffic when A7 + A10 wire. The orchestrator `/website/src/lib/translation-sandwich/parallel-run.ts` is modified at three points (imports, `SandwichRunResult.substrate_layer3_response` field, flag-gated `applyLayer3Injections` call site) to surface the A5 response on `/api/reason`'s composed output when `SUBSTRATE_LAYER3_ENABLED='true'`. Today the env var is **UNSET** in Vercel (the default), so `/api/reason` behaviour is byte-identical to pre-A5 — A5 is operationally ready but not user-visible. Three founder session-open elections committed: **Choice 1(a)** new API route + new library module (cleanest separation; substrate-as-distinct-service framing); **Choice 2(a)** defensive read of future fields for A5.4 R20a distress detection (signal sources: SafetyGate, AC9 `decision==='ESCALATE'`, A7 `distress_signal`; structurally complete, functionally inert today, activates when A7/AC9 wire); **Choice 3(a)** A5.5 prose_mode parameter plumbing only (A6 fills in per-mode templates as its own item). Twenty-eight functional tests pass (FT-1 through FT-12 + AC9-1/2/3 + AC10-1/2/3/4 + AC11-1/2 + INV-1/2/3/3b). All six injection helpers + `applyLayer3Injections` + `isSubstrateLayer3Enabled` invocation-tested via grep on parallel-run.ts: each name appears at both definition and call site per AC4. TypeScript compile passes clean (`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`). PR1 single-endpoint proof on `/api/reason` is **COMPLETE** for A5. A5 implementation status: **Scoped → Designed → Scaffolded → Wired → Verified** in one session (mirrors the A1/A2/A3/A4 precedent for substrate-build sessions). Production state at session close: unchanged. The build arc proceeds to A7 (server-side R20a gate scaffolding) per the indicative session-9 packaging — OR A6 (prose_mode template completion) per founder election at next session-open.

**Reasoning:** A5 is the third-layer R20a defence (per build-sessions cache §"The agreed substrate architecture"): Layer 1 (in-plugin script — fast local), Layer 2 (server-side R20a gate guarding Layer 2 API — A7 surface), Layer 3 (A5 deterministic injection of the distress pass-through into every prose output). Even if Layer 1 and A7 both miss a distress signal, A5 still surfaces appropriate redirection language deterministically — no single point of failure. A5 is also the load-bearing service for the K-category migration (Stage 2): every consumer migrating from bundled-prose to translation-sandwich consumes A5; until A5 is Verified, K-category migration cannot begin. The two-entry-point design (`applyLayer3Injections` vs `generateLayer3Response`) is the load-bearing decision: it lets existing consumers (`/api/reason` via `parallel-run.ts`) wire A5 as a minimum-disruption injection layer on top of their existing `generateProse` call site, while new consumers (the future `/api/substrate/layer3` route called by plugin-originated traffic) get A5 as a complete service that owns prose generation. This sidesteps the double-LLM-call risk that would arise from a single-entry-point design. The defensive-read-of-future-fields choice for A5.4 (the founder's Choice 2(a)) means today A5.4 is structurally complete but functionally inert — `assessment.decision`, `assessment.distress_signal`, and `distress_gate` are all absent on today's Layer2Assessment, so `injectR20aDistressPassthrough` returns null in steady state; the route-level R20a perimeter remains the only active first-line defence. When A7 wires the second-layer gate, A5.4 activates as the third layer. The parameter-plumbing-only choice for A5.5 (Choice 3(a)) respects the staging plan's A6-as-separate-Standard-item framing; the ProseMode enum exists and routes to the existing api_reason template for all four values; A6 will fill in per-mode templates without changing the A5 contract. PR15 bespoke-vs-Anthropic-infrastructure election: bespoke A5 justified — no existing Anthropic primitive (Skills, Sub-agents, Plugins, Managed Agents, MCP servers, SDK patterns) delivers per-consumer Layer 3 prose generation with deterministic R3/R19/R20a/R18a/R18e injection bound to SageReasoning's Layer2Assessment shape. PR16 positioning + dogfood lens: A5 strengthens Character Kernel positioning by carrying R18a category language deterministically into every plugin-originated response; substrate-consultable via `/api/reason` (dogfood relevance: yes — every Layer 3 invocation is a substrate consultation of its own output discipline). Critical Change Protocol completed in full this session: (1) what is changing — A5 scaffolding behind feature flag; (2) what could break — R3 dual-injection (mitigated by separate-field placement), R20a regression if flag flipped before A7 wires (mitigated by route-level perimeter remaining active), TypeScript build (mitigated by clean compile pass); (3) existing sessions — N/A per build-arc no-current-users governing note; (4) rollback Paths A/B/C documented (A: flip flag OFF via Vercel + redeploy ~30s; B: git revert ~5 min; C: N/A no secrets); (5) verification step — 28 functional tests + 12-line invocation grep + clean tsc compile + production-state probe; (6) explicit founder approval received specific to the named risks before commit.

## 2026-05-14 — D-A9-J6-COST-MONITORING-WIRED-2026-05-14

**Decision:** Stage 1 items A9 (cost monitoring on the substrate path) + J6 (R5 cost-shape impact assessment) complete under founder-elected Option B scope. J6 produces a governance assessment at `/operations/r5-cost-shape-impact-assessment-2026-05-14.md` covering the cost-shape change from bundled-engine to substrate to future plugin paradigm, the R5 2x revenue:cost ratio implications, alert threshold recommendations (keep 2.0x multipliers, keep 7-day window, aggregate-only for now, defer per-path split + cap-tracker re-activation), and the Layer 1 cost migration timing expectation. A9 modifies `/website/src/app/api/billing/usage-summary/route.ts` at two surfaces: (i) the LLM-cost source is re-pointed from the prior heuristic (`totalApiCalls × $0.005`) to the substrate path's actual cost capture by summing `layer1_cost_usd_microcents + layer3_cost_usd_microcents` over the period from `translation_sandwich_comparisons`, with defensive fallback to the prior heuristic if the substrate query fails or returns zero rows; (ii) the R5 manifest's "2x rolling 7-day average daily spend" alert is scaffolded — the previously-unused `COST_HEALTH.ROLLING_AVERAGE_ALERT_MULTIPLIER: 2.0` constant is now read by new logic that buckets the prior 7 days of substrate cost by UTC calendar day, computes the prior-7-day average (excluding today), and fires `R5 ALERT` when today's spend ≥ 2.0x average, with a cold-start guard requiring ≥3 days of prior data before firing. Response schema extended: `metrics.cost_source` field (`'substrate' | 'heuristic_fallback'`); `metrics.rolling_seven_day` block (today_usd, prior_seven_day_avg_usd, prior_days_observed, multiplier); `thresholds.rolling_seven_day_alert_multiplier` exposes the constant. A9 implementation status: **Scoped → Designed → Scaffolded → Wired → Verified** in one session. PR1 single-endpoint-proof discipline applied: the `/api/billing/usage-summary` admin route is the single endpoint proving the substrate-cost-source pattern; surface rollout to other consumers (e.g., founder hub cost panel, ops-cost-state context loader) is deferred.

**Reasoning:** R5's two alert rules — the 2x revenue:cost ratio (sentence 1) and the 2x rolling 7-day daily-spend (sentence 2) — were authored against the bundled-engine cost shape pre-M1-CP6. Post-cutover (D-PARALLEL-RUN-CUTOVER-2026-05-08) the translation-sandwich is the sole engine on `/api/reason`, and each request captures Layer 1 + Layer 3 cost on `translation_sandwich_comparisons` rows. The existing `/api/billing/usage-summary` route was still computing LLM cost via the heuristic `totalApiCalls × 0.5 cents`, with the code comment explicitly flagging this should be "refined with actual Anthropic billing data". The rolling-7-day alert was unwired entirely — the `ROLLING_AVERAGE_ALERT_MULTIPLIER` constant existed in `/website/src/lib/stripe.ts` but no code read it. Three branches surfaced at audit-time: (a) narrow re-pointing only; (b) re-pointing + scaffolding the rolling alert; (c) b + re-activating `incrementCostTracker` in the production `runSandwich` path. Founder elected Option B at session-open after audit: closes the two manifest-named R5 gaps cleanly without touching the substrate hot path. Option C was deferred because re-activating the legacy cost tracker would re-enable an M1-CP4 cost cap ($50 / 1000 req / 14 days) on live substrate traffic — those defaults were never updated for the sole-engine state and could short-circuit `/api/reason` traffic without warning. J6's assessment documents this as an explicit deferred decision (Option 1 open question: cap defaults review precedes any production cost-cap activation). PR16 positioning + dogfood lens: A9 + J6 strengthens the substrate-as-honest-substrate positioning (the cost capture per request matches what the manifest requires); the new fields are substrate-consultable via `/api/billing/usage-summary` (admin) and pull-readable for future Sage Ops integration. PR11 authoritative-current-sources rule: at session-open the inbox was scanned for material dated since 2026-05-13; three files matched the date filter (acp.rtf, open ai best practice commerce.rtf, 20260508-104-promptkit-1.md) — none R5/cost-related; consultation findings: no new information that changes the decision. PR12 negative-finding discipline: the prompt's three-branch framing was checked against actual code state at audit-time; found to be more nuanced than presented (Branch (a) and (b) overlap — some R5 alerts exist with heuristic source; the "2x rolling" alert is unwired despite constant existing; Branch (c) describes a real gap but introduces side-effect risk). The recalibration was surfaced honestly to the founder before branch election. PR13 consider-implications five-question assessment: (1) refines prior R5 alert design (heuristic → substrate-derived); (2) refines the unwired rolling-alert constant from `stripe.ts`; (3) affects this session's work directly; (4) affects Stage 3 work (per-path split deferred to Stage 3 kickoff per J6 §4); (5) affects observability discipline only (defensive fallback preserves prior behaviour on query failure).

**Decision:** Adopt the Anthropic-native posture pattern alongside existing multi-stream governance. Five coordinated changes land this session: (1) `/CLAUDE.md` entry-point file created at repo root for Claude Code sessions (~75 lines; points at existing governance heavy-lifters; doesn't replace them); (2) 17 official Anthropic skills from `anthropics/skills` installed at `/.claude/skills/anthropic/` (4 document-skills + 13 example-skills; provenance README at the subfolder; sage-* skills preserved at top level); (3) PR15 amended in `/adopted/project-instructions-snapshot.md` to add Cookbook patterns + Reference agents to the canonical-primitives list and introduce a new OPERATIONAL DISCIPLINE subsection mandating consultation of `.claude/skills/anthropic/` + the agentic-commerce-findings tracker before bespoke election; (4) standing-protocol-cache amended to reference CLAUDE.md + the PR15 amendment date + the new cross-references; (5) features survey refreshed to current state (May 2026), moved from `/drafts/anthropic-features-survey-2026-05-10.md` to `/adopted/anthropic-features-survey-2026-05-14.md`. Plus two complementary 2026-05-14 changes recorded as separate entries: agent-card.json currency check vs A2A v1 (`D-AGENT-CARD-CURRENCY-CHECK-2026-05-14`) and J1 ADR A2A-coordination-layer addendum.

**Reasoning:** The 2026-05-13 Cowork research surfaced two related gaps: (a) the 17 Anthropic-canonical skills were not installed in this repo for Claude Code sessions (6 of the 17 are bundled in Cowork mode but unavailable to Claude Code); (b) PR15 named category labels but didn't mandate consulting specific Anthropic repos. The founder's call after the research was to converge: adopt the Anthropic-canonical CLAUDE.md + Skills pattern where it has clear advantages; preserve the multi-stream governance cache pattern where it has clear advantages. This session executes the convergence. CLAUDE.md is a *pointer* to the cache, not a replacement for it — the cache's tier-declaration / KG-engagement / model-selection / lean+Critical-template selection are not delivered by CLAUDE.md special handling; the cache stays the heavy-lifter. The 17 skills land in a subfolder (`anthropic/`) to coexist cleanly with the 7 sage-* skills already present in `.claude/skills/`. PR15's operational discipline articulates how to satisfy the existing rule, not a new gate — it doesn't add friction; it makes the rule actionable. PR12 negative-finding discipline applied at session-open: the prompt assumed `.claude/skills/` was empty; PR12 caught the 7 sage-* skills and triggered the layout election that drove the subfolder choice. PR11 authoritative-current-sources rule applied: inbox scan at session-open found no material since 2026-05-13; anthropics/skills repo + code.claude.com docs consulted as canonical install guidance. PR13 consider-implications: (1) refines PR15 prior decision; (2) refines features-survey prior recommendation (now adopted as governing reference); (3) affects this session's work directly; (4) affects future-stage work (every subsequent build session now consults .claude/skills/anthropic/ + agentic-commerce-findings); (5) affects operational discipline (cache update, CLAUDE.md auto-load, project-instructions panel paste-sync). PR16 positioning + dogfood lens: strengthens Character Kernel positioning by adopting standard Anthropic primitives without compromising governance discipline; dogfood relevance partial (the convergence decision itself was substrate-mechanism-walkthrough-able but consulted via founder-AI reasoning, not live `/api/reason` call).

The amendment is articulation, not gate-addition — the existing "default is canonical; bespoke needs justification" framing is preserved. ## 2026-05-14 — D-AGENT-CARD-CURRENCY-CHECK-2026-05-14

**Decision:** The SageReasoning agent-card.json at `/website/public/.well-known/agent-card.json` (served LIVE at `sagereasoning.com/.well-known/agent-card.json` since 28 March 2026) reviewed against A2A v1 canonical schema. **Finding:** four load-bearing shape misalignments + missing required fields. **This session's actions:** (1) minor README drift fixed (README line 114 "6 capabilities" → "9 capabilities"; line 240 "5-step quickstart" → "6-step quickstart" + cross-reference to this entry); (2) J1 ADR `/adopted/adr/2026-05-12-substrate-category-character-kernel.md` §"Agentic-commerce-stack adjacency" amended with an A2A-foundational-coordination-protocol addendum (~3 paragraphs) naming A2A as the canonical agent-to-agent coordination layer under the AAIF, recording the A2A v1 alignment status as a forward-looking gap; prior J1 ADR sub-section archived at `/archive/2026-05-14-j1-adr-pre-a2a-addendum.md`. **Deferred:** the actual agent-card.json reshape (capabilities-object-vs-array; skills-objects-vs-strings; authentication.schemes-strings-vs-objects; missing defaultInputModes/defaultOutputModes; custom extensions moved to A2A `extensions` field) to a follow-up Elevated session with its own approval gate.

**Reasoning:** The card declares semantically-correct content but in shapes that A2A v1 consumers won't parse. Specifically: A2A v1 expects `capabilities` to be an OBJECT with booleans (`streaming`, `pushNotifications`, `stateTransitionHistory`); ours is an ARRAY of 9 capability-objects with endpoints. A2A v1 expects `skills` to be an ARRAY of skill-objects with `id`/`name`/`description`/`tags`/`examples`; ours is an array of 10 strings. The shapes are effectively swapped — the substance is right, the structure is wrong. Fixing the structure is a substantive change to a user-facing JSON file served at a well-known path; it deserves its own bounded session with its own approval gate, not an inline cosmetic fix. The minor README drift (capabilities count + quickstart-step count) is descriptive text drift around the file and is safe to correct now. The J1 ADR addendum positions A2A in the architecture in a way that makes the deferred reshape session's context clearer (A2A is the foundational coordination layer; commerce protocols ride on it; Character Kernel publishes its capabilities via A2A discovery). Step 6b applied per founder election; Step 6 deferral applied per founder election.

- `/adopted/adr/2026-05-12-substrate-category-character-kernel.md` — MODIFIED. Header status line extended with 2026-05-14 amendment note. §"Agentic-commerce-stack adjacency" sub-section extended with three paragraphs naming A2A as foundational coordination protocol + recording A2A v1 alignment status.

## 2026-05-14 — D-AGENT-CARD-A2A-V1-RESHAPE-2026-05-14

**Decision:** The SageReasoning agent-card.json at `/website/public/.well-known/agent-card.json` reshaped from its prior mixed shape (Verified-but-A2A-v1-misaligned per `D-AGENT-CARD-CURRENCY-CHECK-2026-05-14`) to **A2A v1 canonical shape**. Single-file reshape, substance preserved, structure aligned to the canonical AgentCard interface per agent2agent.info + a2a-protocol.org. Closes the deferred gap from the predecessor entry.

**Reasoning:** The predecessor session (`D-AGENT-CARD-CURRENCY-CHECK-2026-05-14`) documented four load-bearing shape misalignments + missing required fields, and deferred the reshape to this follow-up Elevated session. PR11 + PR12 spec verification during this session yielded a **load-bearing correction to the predecessor's draft mapping**: the canonical A2A v1 spec places `extensions` **inside** `capabilities` (as `capabilities.extensions[]` of AgentExtension objects), NOT at top level as the predecessor prompt assumed. The agent2agent.info canonical TypeScript interface combined with a2a-protocol.org's published v1 examples (verified via WebSearch) confirmed the nested shape. The reshape therefore: (1) moved the 9 current endpoint-objects from `capabilities` (array) to `skills` (array of skill-objects); (2) created the new top-level `capabilities` object with three boolean flags (all `false` — reflects actual substrate behaviour) + `extensions[]` nested; (3) reshaped `authentication.schemes` from array-of-objects to array-of-strings `["bearer", "none"]` with the descriptive content consolidated into `authentication.credentials`; (4) added required `defaultInputModes: ["application/json"]` + `defaultOutputModes: ["application/json"]`; (5) distributed the prior top-level `skills` (10 strings) + top-level `tags` (12 strings) across per-skill `tags[]` arrays per the founder-approved mapping; (6) moved the three custom blocks (`accessTiers`, `rateLimits`, `quickStart`) into `capabilities.extensions[]` as AgentExtension objects with versioned URIs at `https://sagereasoning.com/extensions/{name}/v1`; (7) retained `endpoint` + `method` as supplementary fields on each skill-object (not in canonical Skill interface but not forbidden; preserves substantive routing info).

## 2026-05-14 — D-LAYER1-SCHEMA-ADDITIONS-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-14

**Decision:** Eight optional carried-context fields added to the open `Layer1Schema` contract as placeholder scaffolding pending mode-spec adoption — four from private mode (`subject_identity_binding`, `reflective_self_report`, `history_window`, `topic_signal`) and four from the Agent Trust Layer Wrapper (`carried_profile`, `profile_provenance`, `peer_agent_assessments`, `objective_function_declaration`). All optional + additive; `validateLayer1Schema` accepts them when present (shape-checked) and still validates a schema without them; Layer 2 defensively tolerates them (passes through untouched, does not yet act on them). Implementation status: Scoped → Designed → Scaffolded → Wired → Verified in one session.

**Reasoning:** The A6 four-mode re-scope (`D-A6-RESCOPED-TO-FOUR-MODE-REDESIGN-2026-05-14`) surfaced eight Layer 1 input fields that private mode and the ATL Wrapper consume; philosophical and standard modes need none. Landing them in one deliberate act versions the open Layer 1 contract once rather than piecemeal across four mode builds, and unblocks all four mode builds at the Layer 1 layer. Founder elected at the session-open gate to land them now as clearly-marked placeholders rather than wait for spec adoption — the fields are optional and unconsumed, so renaming on adoption is cheap.

**Flow-through decision:** Layer 1 still does "text → structured features" unchanged. The eight fields are *carried context* — they are NOT extracted. This session does not wire population: `extractFeatures`, `ExtractInput`, and the Layer 1 LLM system prompt are untouched, so the fields default to absent on every server-side `/api/reason` call (behaviour byte-identical to pre-session). The plugin-auth path (`route.ts` → `validateLayer1Schema` on the request body) already accepts a pre-built `layer1_schema`; that is where the future ATL-wrapper and private-mode build sessions populate the fields. Placeholder types are local (`SubjectIdentityBinding`, `HistoryWindow`; `CarriedProfile` / `ProfileProvenance` / `PeerAgentAssessment` as permissive `Record<string, unknown>`) — NOT imports of `/trust-layer/` types, which sit outside `website/`'s tsconfig root and would break the compile + prematurely lock the contract before spec adoption.

**Open-contract version:** `version` string stays `'layer1-schema-v1'` — optional + additive + backward-compatible is a non-breaking change; the validator accepts v1 with or without the fields. Follows the file's own M1-CP4b precedent. The `version` field doc-comment records the 2026-05-14 addition.

## 2026-05-15 — D-ATL-BRIDGE-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15

**Decision:** The `Layer2Assessment → EvaluatedAction` mapping function — "the bridge" — is built, Wired, and Verified as a new module (`atl-bridge.ts`): a pure, synchronous, deterministic projection that makes the translation-sandwich substrate's signed `Layer2Assessment` the source of the existing `/trust-layer/` build's `EvaluatedAction`. It is the PR1 single-endpoint proof of the substrate↔ATL bridge pattern. The Step 2 design-decision gate resolved three founder-confirmed questions: (1) the **tsconfig-boundary problem** — `EvaluatedAction` + its two dependency enums (`KatorthomaProximityLevel`, `RootPassionId`) are **mirrored** into `website/src` as local target types, because `/trust-layer/` sits outside `website/`'s tsconfig root and cannot be imported; (2) **`receipt_id`** is derived from the Ed25519 signature (`deriveReceiptId` — SHA-256 of the `SignedLayer2Assessment` signature); (3) **`oikeiosis_met` / `oikeiosis_stage`** are taken from the **first** relevant circle (`relevant_circles[0]` — the Layer 2 engine's own "primary circle" convention).

**Reasoning:** The bridge is the central reconciliation move of the ATL Wrapper — it lets the existing `/trust-layer/` window-aggregator / grade-engine / badge infrastructure run on substrate output instead of the superseded bundled engine's "ReasoningReceipts". Built as the simplest reconciliation unit first per PR1; the wrapper, badge, and trajectory components (spec steps 3–7) depend on this mapping existing. **tsconfig-boundary decision:** `website/tsconfig.json`'s `include` globs are rooted at `website/`; there is no root-level or `/trust-layer/` tsconfig; importing `EvaluatedAction` from `/trust-layer/` would pull ~4,200 lines of never-strict-compiled code into `tsc`. Mirroring the target type is the only Step-2 option fitting this session's Standard-risk, PR1 scope, and is consistent with `/trust-layer/`'s own established self-containment pattern (its BUILD-LOG records re-declaring `KatorthomaProximityLevel` etc. rather than coupling to `website/src`). Bringing `/trust-layer/` under the tsconfig / relocating its types / a shared package were all rejected as structural changes larger than the bridge. **Step 1 survey finding:** four `EvaluatedAction` fields are not on `Layer2Assessment` and cannot be (it is idempotent by design — no clock, no identity, no signature) — `agent_id` (which the spec's Component 1 mapping table omits entirely; the survey surfaced it), `evaluated_at`, `skill_id`, and the `receipt_id` material; all four are supplied via a `BridgeContext` parameter, so the bridge signature is `(Layer2Assessment, BridgeContext) → EvaluatedAction`. **PR15:** an Anthropic-canonical primitive was considered — the `.claude/skills/anthropic/` skills + the canonical-primitive list — and rejected; no skill or primitive delivers a deterministic in-process TypeScript type-projection function (the closest, `claude-api`, concerns API usage; the spec flags multi-agent orchestration for Component 5, spec step 5, not the bridge); bespoke is correct. **PR11:** no `/inbox/` files dated since the predecessor session; the agentic-commerce findings tracker carries no F-finding targeting the bridge (F4 targets the wrapper — spec step 5 — not this session).

**Files touched:**
- `/website/src/lib/substrate/atl-bridge.ts` — NEW. The bridge: `mapLayer2AssessmentToEvaluatedAction` (the projection), `deriveReceiptId` + `RECEIPT_ID_PREFIX` (the SHA-256-of-signature receipt_id convention), the `BridgeContext` input type, and the mirrored `EvaluatedAction` / `KatorthomaProximityLevel` / `RootPassionId` target types. Consumes `Layer2Assessment` (type-only) + `node:crypto`'s `createHash`. No existing file modified; not wired to any route.
- `/website/src/lib/substrate/__tests__/atl-bridge.test.ts` — NEW. 31 assertions (receipt_id derivation; full-assessment mapping; context fields; oikeiosis first-circle selection; null narrowing; minimal assessment; determinism + no-mutation invariants; shape-validity for `window-aggregator.ts`). Invokes `mapLayer2AssessmentToEvaluatedAction` — PR2 build-to-wire verification immediate.
- `/website/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` — touched by `tsc --noEmit` (incremental-build cache; tracked; routinely changes when tsc runs).
- `/operations/decision-log.md` — this entry appended.
