## 2026-05-15 — D-ATL-SCORE-ARCHITECTURE-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15

**Decision:** The substrate score-computation module — `score-architecture.ts` — is built, Wired, and Verified as a new module: a pure, synchronous, deterministic projection from a `Layer2Assessment` (+ a `ScoreContext`) to a single `SubstrateScore` (the kathekon gate outcome, the seven score components, the scalar 0-100 value, the validity flag, the cap rules, the precision band, the confidence field). It is the PR1 single-endpoint proof of the score pattern, and the load-bearing dependency for three downstream consumers — the Layer 3 agent-mode rendering (ATL Wrapper Component 2), philosophical mode's deferred score sections (`D-PHILOSOPHICAL-MODE-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-14`, PR7), and standard mode's score sections. The Step 2 design-decision gate resolved the score-formula details the superseded agent-mode spec left to "build session computes", plus one finding that corrects the superseded spec against the real Layer 2 type (see Reasoning). Founder elected the score-module-only scope at Step 0; the agent-mode rendering and the philosophical-mode score-wiring are NOT built this session — they follow against this now-Verified module.

**Reasoning:** The score architecture was specified only in the now-superseded agent-mode spec (`/archive/2026-05-14_agent-mode-response-spec-superseded.md`), with formulas explicitly marked "build session computes". Building it here — the natural home, per the predecessor close — closes the carried-forward PR7 deferral's revisit condition ("the substrate score architecture reaches Scaffolded") and unblocks standard mode's score sections, which the standard-mode spec flags as depending on the same architecture. Built as the simplest score unit first per PR1, the same session shape as `atl-bridge.ts` and `philosophical-mode-service.ts`. **Step 2 design-decision gate (founder pre-approved the recommended options):** (1) **module location** — new file `website/src/lib/substrate/score-architecture.ts` + test, mirroring the bridge / philosophical-mode file shape; (2) **signature** — `computeSubstrateScore(assessment: Layer2Assessment, context: ScoreContext): SubstrateScore`, the bridge pattern; `ScoreContext` carries `justification_source` (required — the kathekon gate's primary input, not on `Layer2Assessment`; `philosophical-mode-service.ts` hard-codes `justification_source: null` precisely because this build had not happened) and `declared_motivation_passion?` (`'detected'` / `'clean'` / absent — the module consumes a pre-classified verdict; the actual passion-language detection on free text is an upstream agent-mode / Layer-1-normalisation concern, superseded spec open questions 2-4, out of scope here); (3) **structural-passion per-passion base = 1.25** → stage penalties {phantasia 1.25, synkatathesis 2.5, horme 3.75, praxis 5.0}, summed, floored at -15 — a single praxis-stage passion = -5, one-third of the channel cap, honouring "passion location is the load-bearing signal, not count"; (4) **value-error aggregation** — trigger on `treated_as !== 'indifferent'`, penalty by `axia` (high -8 / moderate -5 / low -2), summed, floored at -15; (5) **cap + multiplier arithmetic** — `(baseline 55 + components) × quality_multiplier`, rounded (round-half-up), then `clamp(5, 100)` on the confirmed-NORMAL path or `min(rounded, cap)` then `clamp(0, 100)` on a capped path (makes the spec's stated [5, 100] range exact); (6) **precision band** — base ±5, +5 per major uncertainty signal (marginal quality / justification ≠ engine_constructed / motivation unclear / is_kathekon null), capped ±20; calibrated so the "precision_band > ±15 → PROVISIONAL" backstop only fires on paths the gate has already made PROVISIONAL. **Finding that corrects the superseded spec (Step 2 decision 3):** the superseded spec's validity-flag table says `motivation_classification: null → PROVISIONAL`, but the real `Layer2Assessment` type defines `null` as *"no praxis-stage action observed"* — a genuine N/A, not a data gap. Taking the spec literally would cap the majority of perfectly-determinable assessments at 50, defeating the score's purpose. Adopted reading: PROVISIONAL fires on `unclear_pending_clarification` only. **Decision:** The Layer 3 agent-mode rendering — ATL Wrapper Component 2, "Component 2 proper" at the per-assessment level — is built, Wired, and Verified as a new module (`agent-mode-service.ts`): a pure, synchronous, deterministic projection from a `Layer2Assessment` + a `ScoreContext` to a dual-audience output — the in-loop machine-readable JSON (`AgentModeResponse`) the wrapped agent consumes, and the per-assessment human-readable Markdown rendering the developer reads — both carrying the six mandatory wraps (R3 / R19c / R19d / R20a / R18a / R18e), both deterministic with no LLM call. It is the PR1 single-endpoint proof of the agent-mode rendering pattern, wired as a new `'atl_wrapper'` case in the proven `renderLayer3Mode` dispatch. It is the first consumer of the now-Verified `score-architecture.ts`. Founder elected the agent-mode-rendering-only scope at Step 0 (the recommended option); the philosophical-mode score-wiring (the PR7 deferral) was NOT done this session — it follows as a fast follow against this now-Verified rendering as a worked second consumer of the score module.

Built as the simplest rendering unit first per PR1, the same survey-then-build session shape as `atl-bridge.ts`, `score-architecture.ts`, and `philosophical-mode-service.ts`. **Step 2 design-decision gate (founder pre-approved the recommended options):** (1) **renderer location** — new file `website/src/lib/substrate/agent-mode-service.ts` + test; `renderLayer3Mode` in `philosophical-mode-service.ts` gains a `case 'atl_wrapper'` delegating to `renderAgentMode`; `Layer3RenderMode` extended with the reserved value `'atl_wrapper'` (confirmed against the spec); `renderLayer3Mode` gains function overloads so each mode's return type stays precise (existing `'philosophical'` callers are unchanged — their `.json` is still a `PhilosophicalModeResponse`, not a union); the runtime import graph stays acyclic (philosophical → agent-mode is a value import; agent-mode → philosophical is a type-only, erased import). ## 2026-05-15 — D-ATL-WRAPPER-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15

**Decision:** The Agent Trust Layer Wrapper's Components 1 + 4 — the carried-profile mechanism + trajectory awareness (ATL Wrapper spec step 5) — are built, Wired, and Verified as a new module (`atl-wrapper.ts`): a synchronous, deterministic accumulator (`accumulate` — pure) + aggregator (`computeTrajectory` — deterministic modulo the ISO-timestamp fields the ported `/trust-layer/` functions stamp) that takes an agent's substrate consultations, maps each `Layer2Assessment` via the now-Verified `atl-bridge.ts`, accumulates the `EvaluatedAction`s into a `CarriedProfile`, drives the ported `computeWindowSnapshot` + `evaluateGradeTransition` to produce a `WindowSnapshot` + grade transition, and emits the `carried_profile` / `profile_provenance` payloads for the agent's next `Layer1Schema` input. The `/trust-layer/` ↔ `website` integration boundary is **resolved** — closing the carried-forward open question from `D-ATL-BRIDGE-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15`. Founder elected the Components-1+4 scope at Step 0 and pre-approved all four Step 2 design decisions as recommended.

**Reasoning:** ATL Wrapper spec step 5 — the genuine next step after the bridge (step 2), the score architecture (step 3 dep), the agent-mode rendering (step 3), and the Layer 1 schema additions (step 4, already Verified 2026-05-14). The wrapper is the continuity-bearing structure around the per-assessment substrate calls — what the private mentor is to a human. It is mostly *wiring already-Verified pieces*, not net-new design. **Step 2 design-decision gate (founder pre-approved all four recommended options):** (1) **the `/trust-layer/` integration boundary** — option (a), PORT the 5-file dependency closure of `computeWindowSnapshot` + `evaluateGradeTransition` (`types/accreditation.ts`, `types/evaluation.ts`, `accreditation/accreditation-record.ts`, `evaluation-window/window-aggregator.ts`, `grade-engine/grade-transition-engine.ts` — ~1,700 lines, NOT the full ~4,200) into `website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/`, preserving the directory structure so every relative import resolves verbatim, each file a KEEP-IN-SYNC mirror with a banner. Rejected (b) bringing all of `/trust-layer/` under `website/`'s tsconfig — a build-config change (Elevated) that pulls never-strict-compiled code (incl. the badge / authority / progression files the wrapper does not need) under `tsc --strict`; and (c) a narrow tsconfig — same drawbacks, fiddlier. Porting stays **Standard** risk, is consistent with the bridge's mirroring precedent + `/trust-layer/`'s own self-containment pattern (its BUILD-LOG records the same choice), and the wrapper needs the *logic* of two functions, not their types — the bridge's type-only mirror would not have sufficed. (2) **the carried-profile data structure** — `CarriedProfile` carries `evaluated_actions: readonly EvaluatedAction[]`, `total_actions_evaluated`, the seeded `accreditation_record` (`evaluateGradeTransition` needs a prior record — the carried profile is where it lives; a fresh agent seeds at reflexive / pre_progress / all-emerging — real onboarding is spec open question 7, deferred), and `regressing_check_count` (the grade engine's downgrade-hysteresis input, maintained by `computeTrajectory`: a regressing snapshot increments it, any non-regressing snapshot resets it, a grade change resets it); module location `website/src/lib/substrate/atl-wrapper.ts` + test, mirroring the bridge / score / agent-mode file shape. (3) **storage** — wrapper-side carriage, NO server-side persistence for the carried profile this session (spec open question 2; the badge's server persistence is step 6); every `atl-wrapper.ts` function is a pure transform over a `CarriedProfile` VALUE the caller holds. (4) **`carried_profile` ↔ `Layer1Schema` contract** — the payload carries the aggregated `WindowSnapshot` (bounded in size; what trajectory-aware Layer 2 assessment needs), NOT the raw `EvaluatedAction[]` (grows unbounded); `senecan_grade` + `typical_proximity` surfaced alongside as the headline; both `CarriedProfilePayload` + `ProfileProvenancePayload` are plain JSON-serialisable objects that round-trip through `validateLayer1Schema`'s permissive `carried_profile` / `profile_provenance` `assertObject` checks (test PAY-5 confirms). **Bridge consolidation (Step 2 sub-decision, founder-elected):** `atl-bridge.ts` is repointed — its local `MIRRORED TARGET TYPES` block (`EvaluatedAction` + `KatorthomaProximityLevel` + `RootPassionId`, ~50 lines) is removed; it now imports the CANONICAL `EvaluatedAction` from the ported `trust-layer/types/` and re-exports all three so its consumers are unaffected. One definition in `website/src`; the bridge's `atl-bridge.test.ts` 31/0 confirms zero behaviour change. **Step 1 survey finding (clock read — surfaced, accepted):** the ported `computeWindowSnapshot` + `evaluateGradeTransition` stamp ISO timestamps (`computed_at` / `updated_at` / `grade_since` / `last_evaluation`) from the system clock — the prompt's ideal of "no clock read beyond `BridgeContext`" does not hold for the ported `/trust-layer/` logic. Resolution: port verbatim (do not modify the ported functions), `accumulate` is fully pure, `computeTrajectory` is deterministic in every field EXCEPT those ISO-timestamp fields; the test (DET-1) asserts determinism modulo timestamps. **`agent_id`** is carried as a wrapper-supplied opaque string (spec open question 8; authenticating it is A10, deferred); `accumulate` forces the bridge context's `agent_id` to the carried profile's — a light gaming-defence touch. **R17e:** explicitly does NOT apply — an agent's reasoning-pattern profile is not an intimate human vulnerability (the load-bearing distinction from private mode); no R17e filter in `atl-wrapper.ts`. **R4:** the grade engine's `UPGRADE_THRESHOLDS` / `DOWNGRADE_THRESHOLDS` are module-private inside the ported `grade-transition-engine.ts` — never exported, never returned; a `TransitionResult` exposes only the R4-respecting `AccreditationRecord` + plain-English summaries. **PR15:** an Anthropic-canonical primitive was considered — the 17 skills at `.claude/skills/anthropic/` + the canonical-primitive list — and rejected; none delivers an in-process deterministic TypeScript accumulator/aggregator (the same finding as the bridge / score / agent-mode builds; `claude-api` concerns getting an LLM to *produce* structured output, the inverse). Multi-agent orchestration (a named Anthropic primitive) is relevant to Component 5 pattern 3 — NOT this session. Bespoke is correct. **PR11:** no `/inbox/` files dated since the predecessor session; the agentic-commerce findings tracker carries no F-finding targeting this session (F4 — "the wrapper's carried profile is an AP2-style accumulated-mandate structure" — is contextually relevant but its target session is A12, a contextual note only).

## 2026-05-15 — D-ATL-ITERATION-PATTERNS-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15

**Decision:** The Agent Trust Layer Wrapper's Component 5 — the three iteration patterns (sequential loop / parallel evaluation / multi-agent orchestration; ATL Wrapper spec §"Component 5") — is built, Wired, and Verified as a new module (`atl-iteration-patterns.ts`): pure / deterministic-modulo-timestamps orchestration of the already-Verified `atl-wrapper.ts` (Components 1 + 4), `agent-mode-service.ts` (Component 2 rendering) and the ported `/trust-layer/` `buildAccreditationPayload`. `runSequentialStep` / `runSequentialLoop` implement pattern 1 (and finally implement the grade-check *cadence* `atl-wrapper.ts` deliberately left to Component 5); `evaluateInParallel` / `accumulateChosen` implement pattern 2; `toPeerAgentAssessments` / `runOrchestrationStep` implement pattern 3. After this session every ATL Wrapper component except the badge (Component 3) is real. Founder pre-elected the all-three-patterns scope at Step 0 and pre-approved the four Step 2 design decisions as recommended (per the session prompt's "Proceed accepting the recommended options").

**Reasoning:** ATL Wrapper spec step 5's successor — Component 5 is the last component before the badge. It is mostly orchestration of already-Verified pieces, not net-new design. **Step 2 design-decision gate (founder pre-approved all four as recommended):** (1) **PR15 — pattern 3 is bespoke.** The load-bearing PR15 consult evaluated Anthropic's multi-agent-orchestration primitive (Claude Managed Agents → Multiagent sessions; public beta, `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta header — consulted at `platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multi-agent`). Finding: that primitive is the *runtime substrate an orchestrator agent runs on* — a coordinator delegating to a roster of ≤20 agents in context-isolated session threads; it does not accumulate reasoning-quality trajectory, do Stoic assessment, or populate `peer_agent_assessments`. The ATL Wrapper *wraps* such an orchestrator. Complementary, not competing → bespoke is correct (the same finding as the bridge / score / agent-mode / wrapper builds: no Anthropic primitive delivers in-process deterministic TS orchestration of deterministic modules). `.claude/skills/anthropic/` (17 skills) carries none matching multi-agent-orchestration scope. (2) **Open question 4 — parallel-evaluation profile accumulation: only the CHOSEN candidate feeds the carried profile.** The carried profile is the record of *committed* reasoning, and the grade thresholds (`min_actions` 20/40/60/80) are calibrated against committed decisions, not deliberation breadth; the agent reasoned once (one decision point) evaluating N candidates. `evaluateInParallel` produces the ranked N-candidate comparison (decision-support, no profile mutation); `accumulateChosen` is the separate explicit step that folds the chosen candidate in via `runSequentialStep`. (3) **Open question 5 — orchestration depth + grade propagation: depth-1 posture; grade carried as data, not propagated.** `toPeerAgentAssessments` builds `peer_agent_assessments` from a *flat* peer list and does not recurse into peers' peers (`MAX_ORCHESTRATION_DEPTH = 1`) — mirroring Anthropic's own primitive ("depth > 1 is ignored"). A peer's grade is carried as data in `peer_agent_assessments`; the orchestrator's own `CarriedProfile` + grade are computed *only* from the orchestrator's own accumulated `EvaluatedActions` (`runOrchestrationStep` delegates the orchestrator's own accumulation to `runSequentialStep`) — a peer's grade transition influences future orchestrator assessments only by being in the orchestrator's Layer 1 input. (4) **Module shape — a single `atl-iteration-patterns.ts` (+ test)**, mirroring the `atl-wrapper.ts` / `atl-bridge.ts` file shape; the three patterns are closely coupled, share types, and are thin orchestration — three modules would fragment closely-coupled code. **PR13 five-question check on the PR15 finding:** it does not contradict a prior decision; it refines open question 5 (the depth-1 precedent); it confirms pattern 3 is bespoke in-flight; it is a forward pointer for any future live-agent-loop work; no operational-discipline impact. **PR11:** no `/inbox/` files dated since the predecessor session (newest 2026-05-13); the agentic-commerce findings tracker carries no F-finding targeting this session (F4 is contextual only, target A12).

## 2026-05-15 — D-ATL-BADGE-SCHEMA-PERSISTENCE-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15

**Decision:** The Agent Trust Layer Wrapper's Component 3 — the badge / accreditation — has its **foundation built, Wired, and Verified** as ATL Wrapper spec step 6a (the recommended split scope; the public verification endpoint is held to step 6b). Three things landed: (1) the **`agent_accreditation` + `grade_history` schema subset** of the DRAFT 5-table `/trust-layer/schema/trust-layer-schema-REVIEW.sql` is approved and produced as a runnable, idempotent migration (`website/supabase-agent-accreditation-migration.sql`) for the founder to run via the Supabase SQL Editor; (2) the two un-ported `/trust-layer/` badge files (`public-endpoint.ts`, `accreditation-card.ts`) are **ported** into `website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/` as KEEP-IN-SYNC verbatim mirrors; (3) a new **persistence layer** (`atl-accreditation-store.ts`) maps `AccreditationRecord` ⇄ the `agent_accreditation` row and `GradeChangeEvent` ⇄ the `grade_history` row, with `lookupAccreditationRecord` shaped exactly as `handleAccreditationLookup`'s injected `lookupFn` seam. `trust-layer-bridge.ts` is **retired** (its disposition decided; the deletion itself is delegated to the founder's `git rm` — see Open questions). No route is wired this session (PR1 — the persistence layer reaches Verified as library code first). Founder pre-elected the 6a scope at Step 0 and pre-approved the five Step 2 design decisions as recommended (per the session prompt's "Proceed accepting the recommended options").

**Reasoning:** ATL Wrapper spec step 6 — the last remaining component; after the badge, every ATL Wrapper component is real and the trajectory-enriched developer hand-back report becomes buildable. The badge is the **first server-side persistence in the ATL arc** (Components 1, 2, 4, 5 are all wrapper-side carriage), which is why it is higher-risk than its predecessors and why the 6a/6b split matters. **Step 2 design-decision gate (founder pre-approved all five as recommended):** (1) **Schema subset** — approve + run only `agent_accreditation` (the public endpoint must query it) + `grade_history` (the grade-change audit trail, fed by `buildGradeChangeEvent`); defer `evaluated_actions` (Component 5 kept the carried profile wrapper-side per `D-ATL-ITERATION-PATTERNS-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-15` — the raw action list has no server-side home and need not get one for the badge), `onboarding_results` (spec open question 7), `progression_sessions` (spec open question 1). One survey improvement over the verbatim DRAFT: `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` guards added before each `CREATE POLICY` so the whole script is re-runnable, not only the `CREATE TABLE` statements. (2) **Porting plan** — `public-endpoint.ts` → `trust-layer/accreditation/public-endpoint.ts` (existing dir), `accreditation-card.ts` → `trust-layer/card/accreditation-card.ts` (new `card/` dir); verbatim copies under KEEP-IN-SYNC banners, matching the 5-file ported-closure pattern. **Step 1 survey finding — dependency closure is clean:** both badge files import only `../types/accreditation` + `./accreditation-record`, both already in the ported closure — `authority-mapper.ts` is NOT needed (`proximityToAuthority` is already in the ported `accreditation-record.ts`). No new dependency files ported. (3) **Persistence-layer shape** — `atl-accreditation-store.ts`: pure mappers (`accreditationRecordToRow` / `rowToAccreditationRecord` / `rowToStoreMetadata` / `gradeChangeEventToRow` / `buildInitialGradeHistoryRow`) + async store functions over `supabaseAdmin` (`lookupAccreditationRecord` / `upsertAccreditationRecord` / `appendGradeHistory` / `appendInitialGradeHistory`). **Three mapping seams (Step 1 survey findings):** the nested `dimension_levels` object flattens to/from four flat columns; `verification_url` + `disclaimer` are derived constants, not columns — dropped on write, reconstructed on read; `tier` + `regressing_check_count` are store-only columns with no `AccreditationRecord` counterpart (`regressing_check_count` lives on the wrapper's `CarriedProfile`) — write-time options, read back via `rowToStoreMetadata`. (5) **Route reconciliation — recorded, not built.** `/api/badge/[id]` already exists but is the V3 *document-evaluation* SVG badge (keyed by an evaluation `id`, serving `document_evaluations_v3` / `document_scores`) — an entirely different concern. Recommendation carried to 6b: a NEW `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` route; leave `/api/badge/[id]` untouched. **KG1:** the persistence layer's five-rule posture is stated in the module header — no self-calls; all DB writes awaited + errors thrown (no fire-and-forget); no redirects; no background work; no file loaders. **KG7:** `passions_persisting` JSONB — `accreditationRecordToRow` passes the `PersistingPassion[]` array directly to the Supabase client (never `JSON.stringify`); `rowToAccreditationRecord` reads it back with an `Array.isArray` guard (a double-serialised string fails the guard and yields `[]` — the KG7 failure mode — rather than iterating characters); expected `jsonb_typeof` is `'array'`, verified by the founder after the first write (the probe is in Founder Verification, deferred to step 6b's first write). **PR15:** `.claude/skills/anthropic/` (17 skills) + the canonical-primitive list were consulted — none substitutes for a Next.js-route + Supabase persistence layer; `mcp-builder` is a forward pointer for R18c interoperability (the verification surface could later be an MCP server) but not this session. ## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-PUBLIC-ACCREDITATION-ENDPOINT-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Wired the public verification endpoint `GET /api/accreditation/[agent_id]` — the named public surface of ATL Wrapper spec §"Component 3 — The Badge / Accreditation" (Adopted 2026-05-14). The route plugs the 6a `lookupAccreditationRecord` straight into the 6a `handleAccreditationLookup` and serves the agent's R4-compliant `AccreditationPayload` (default) or the displayable `AccreditationCard` (`?format=card`). After this entry, **every ATL Wrapper component (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is real end-to-end** — Component 3 (the badge) is now serviceable from anywhere on the public internet. PR1 single-endpoint discipline satisfied (the read endpoint is the single new surface; the batch endpoint is intentionally not wired and is deferred under PR7).

**Reasoning:** Component 3's persistence layer reached Verified at 6a; this 6b session is the public route that exposes it. Step 0 — scope confirmed (read endpoint only) and risk classification confirmed Critical (a new public route + deployment surface) by the founder. Step 2 — seven design decisions consolidated and approved as recommended: (1) `AccreditationPayload` default + `?format=card` for serialized card; (2) `ACCREDITATION_RESPONSE_HEADERS` directly (designed for this surface; carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` + 5-min cache + `X-Accreditation-Disclaimer` header — `publicCorsHeaders()` would restrict to sagereasoning.com origins which defeats the verifiability use-case); (3) status → HTTP mapping `ok`/200, `not_found`/404, `expired`/200-with-data, `error`/400; (4) `documentation_url: 'https://sagereasoning.com/limitations'` injected on every response (the R19c/R19d page at `/website/src/app/limitations/page.tsx` is live — no placeholder needed); (5) `verification_url` reconciliation — leave as-is (the human-facing `/accreditation/` page is future work, distinct from the `/api/accreditation/` route); (6) seed-SQL + cleanup-`DELETE` pair provided for the founder's post-deploy URL check; (7) batch endpoint deferred (PR1 / PR7). Plus a testability factor: `buildAccreditationResponse(result)` extracted as a pure function so PR2 invocation testing exercises all four discriminated `AccreditationEndpointResponse` variants without a Supabase round-trip. The full Critical Change Protocol (0c-ii) was completed visibly in the conversation; the founder explicitly approved against the five named risks (CORS misconfiguration / no rate limit / R4 leak / Supabase error → 500 / Vercel build failure) before any code was written. PR15 consult — `.claude/skills/anthropic/` reviewed; `mcp-builder` is a forward pointer for R18c interoperability (the verification surface could later also be exposed as an MCP server) but the spec's named surface for 6b is the Next.js route, and no Anthropic primitive substitutes for it — bespoke election justified. PR11 — no `/inbox/` files dated since the predecessor brainstorm close (2026-05-15 15:57); F1–F4 in the agentic-commerce findings tracker all target later sessions (FPE-5, Stage 4 G3, A6/A10/A12) — none target 6b.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-ITEMS-1-3-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for ATL Wrapper items 1, 2, and 3 (the post-6b enhancement arc, step 2 of 8 per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Four sub-designs:
- **A — `deliberation_breadth`.** New fifth `BridgeContext` field `candidates_considered: number` (wrapper-supplied; no agent-declared fallback) maps onto `EvaluatedAction`. Layer2Assessment stays idempotent — the signal lives only where the wrapper holds it. A `DeliberationBreadth` enum (`intuited` / `deliberated` / `multi_branch_deliberated`) is derived at aggregation time using N=1 / N=2 / N≥3 thresholds — tunable later without data migration. `WindowSnapshot` gains `deliberation_breadth_distribution` + `typical_deliberation_breadth`, mirroring `proximity_distribution` / `typical_proximity`. `AccreditationRecord` + `AccreditationPayload` gain `typical_deliberation_breadth` — versions the R18c-interoperable schema by one short field; R18a-honest observable credential.
- **B — `carried_candidates`.** NEW slot on `CarriedProfile`, persistent across iterations, top-K capped (K from D). Shape: `{ layer1_input, layer2_assessment, rank, considered_at }[]` (Layer 3 omitted — re-derivable via `renderAgentMode`). Becomes a fifth wrapper-populated optional `Layer1Schema` field alongside `carried_profile` / `peer_agent_assessments` / `objective_function_declaration` / `profile_provenance`. Additive + backward-compatible (optional); versioned change to the open Layer 1 contract — Rule A (licensing gate) noted for the items 1–3 build session.
- **C — tree-search composition.** Doc + small helper. New file `atl-tree-search-adapter.ts` exposes `createSubstrateEvaluator(bridgeContextProvider)` returning a per-node evaluator function. Per-node contract is the EXISTING substrate API `(Layer1Input) => Layer2Assessment` — with A + B applied, `Layer1Schema` already carries all per-node context the tree-search algorithm needs to thread through. New section in `agent-trust-layer-wrapper-spec.md` documents the contract with pseudocode for MCTS / BFS / ToT (no reference implementations) + a short subsection distinguishing in-process tree search (substrate-as-per-node-evaluator) from multi-agent tree-like behaviour (Anthropic orchestration as runtime substrate; ATL wraps the orchestrator per Pattern 3).
- **D — top-K retention.** Helper + doc. New helper `pruneToTopK(candidates, k, comparator?)` (in `atl-iteration-patterns.ts` or a sibling — build-session decision). Default comparator: hybrid — agent's `objective_function_declaration` (Layer1Schema gaming-defence field) if declared, else `katorthoma_proximity` rank. Default K = 5, agent-overridable. Applies to the Decision B `carried_candidates` slot.

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the items 1–3 build session (step 3 of the post-6b arc; `code-elevated` risk classification expected).

**Reasoning:** The 2026-05-15 brainstorm confirmed items 1, 2, 3 in principle and named four open design questions per item. This session locks each. Cross-cutting rationale: (1) `Layer2Assessment` is idempotent by design (atl-bridge.ts module header — no clock, no identity, no signature inside; same Layer1Schema in → byte-identical assessment out), so any per-decision wrapper-owned signal must travel through `BridgeContext` onto `EvaluatedAction`, not into Layer2Assessment. This forces A's location. (2) Pattern 2's founder-closed open question 4 (atl-iteration-patterns.ts — "only the chosen candidate feeds the carried profile") separates the committed-reasoning record from working-set state. So live candidates need a SEPARATE slot on the carried profile, not a merge into the committed accumulation. This frames B. (3) PR15 — Anthropic's multi-agent-orchestration primitive was found complementary, not competing, in the iteration-patterns build; the same finding holds for tree-search composition. The ATL is the per-node evaluator; tree search stays agent-side. This frames C. (4) Verifiers care whether an agent habitually deliberates vs intuits — the `deliberation_breadth` signal is R18a-honest observable reasoning and earns its place on the badge.

## 2026-05-16 — D-HAND-BACK-REPORT-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Built and Verified (at type-check) the trajectory-enriched developer hand-back report — step 4 of 8 in the post-6b arc. New module `/website/src/lib/substrate/agent-hand-back-report.ts` exposes `renderAgentHandBackReport(input): HandBackReportResult` (a pure, synchronous, deterministic Markdown renderer over `CarriedProfile` + `SequentialStepResult[]` / `OrchestrationStepResult[]` + `WindowSnapshot` + `AccreditationPayload`). The report is the developer-facing companion to the existing bespoke `renderAgentMode` (Component 2 in-loop rendering) — the second of the three audience surfaces named in the wrapper spec §"The report the agent hands back to the developer". The third (the public accreditation endpoint) is already Live since 6b.

**Six design-decision-gate elections (Step 1, all founder-confirmed at recommended):**

1. **Module location.** Sibling to `agent-mode-service.ts` at `/website/src/lib/substrate/agent-hand-back-report.ts` (flat structure preserved; no directory created).
2. **Output shape.** Markdown string. Returns `{ markdown: string }`. One rendered document the developer pastes into their tooling, prints, or version-controls.
3. **Section structure.** Five fixed sections matching the spec's five bullets (Decisions; Trajectory; Grade/authority/badge; Persisting passions; Peer agents — last shown only when applicable), plus a Section 1.5 "Still under consideration" for the carried_candidates working set.
4. **Deliberation_breadth visualisation.** Per-action label (with N when > 1) in Section 1's decisions + session-headline `typical_deliberation_breadth` line in Section 2's trajectory + `deliberation_breadth_distribution` line.
5. **Carried_candidates visualisation.** "Still under consideration" subsection — always render (empty-state language when the slot is empty so the developer never wonders if the section exists). Top-K with rank, proximity (R4-safe — only the qualitative level crosses), and considered_at timestamp.
6. **Orchestrator branch rendering.** Section 5 renders only when at least one step in `steps[]` had a non-empty `peer_agent_assessments` (per Q6). Empty-state hidden. Each peer rendered with latest observation (latest grade / proximity / authority_level / direction_of_travel / typical_deliberation_breadth + a "latest-rendering held / not held" note).

**Mandatory wraps (developer audience):**
- **R3** — `ACCREDITATION_DISCLAIMER` rendered verbatim in the signoff (sourced from `record.disclaimer`).
- **R18a** — Character Kernel category-framing in the preamble (identical-in-substance to the J1 ADR's language).
- **R19c** — limitations page URL in the preamble (`https://sagereasoning.com/limitations`).
- **R19d** — developer-audience mirror principle ("mirror onto your wrapped agent's reasoning patterns, not a verdict on you as a developer").
- **R18e** — NOT engaged at the report level. The report consumes structured fields only; it does not quote raw Layer 3 prose, so each per-rendering Article-50 transparency wrap stays in its rendering.
- **R20a** — NOT a new wrap. Any R20a passthrough during the session is naturally reflected in the EvaluatedAction's existing fields; the consumer-side surface stays at the per-rendering level (renderAgentMode).
- **R17e** — does NOT apply to agent profiles (wrapper spec §"R-rule engagement"; load-bearing distinction from private mode).

**Files touched:**
- `/website/src/lib/substrate/agent-hand-back-report.ts` (NEW) — the public renderer + module-private section/helper functions + R-wrap constants + types (`HandBackReportInput`, `HandBackOptions`, `HandBackReportResult`). Pure, synchronous, deterministic given a supplied snapshot.
- `/website/src/lib/substrate/__tests__/agent-hand-back-report.test.ts` (NEW) — covers RENDER-1..8 + DET-1 + R3-1 + R4-1 + R18a-1 (PR2 build-to-wire immediate). Plain-assertion harness, modelled on the existing atl-tree-search-adapter / atl-wrapper / atl-iteration-patterns test pattern.

**Risk classification:** **Elevated** under 0d-ii — new library module, new test file. New module is imported by NO route this session — `/api/reason`, `/api/substrate/layer3`, `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]`, `/api/public-key` are byte-identical to pre-session state. AC5 not engaged (no R20a perimeter change). AC7 not engaged (no auth / session / encryption surface). PR6 not engaged (no R20a / distress-classifier surface). Critical Change Protocol not engaged. PR1 single-build proof: the renderer is proved on one module + one test file this session.

The atl-wrapper, atl-iteration-patterns, atl-bridge, atl-tree-search-adapter, and trust-layer ported files are unaffected. The substrate's existing route surfaces are byte-identical (the new module is imported by no route). No Supabase changes this session — nothing to revert there.

**What could break (Elevated additions):**

Tested by tsc --noEmit clean across the whole `tsconfig.json` scope.
2. **R4 boundary violation in the output** — an internal threshold or per-dimension confidence value crosses into the rendered report. *Mitigation:* the report sources its grade/authority/badge data from `buildAccreditationPayload(record)` (the R4-compliant subset) and only the public-shape fields of the WindowSnapshot (no `dimension_detail`). R4-1 test asserts the absence of seven internal threshold names + four internal record-only fields.
3. **Determinism violation** — the renderer reads the clock or uses randomness. *Mitigation:* the renderer reads no clock and uses no randomness; the optional `snapshot` parameter exists exactly for the deterministic-test path; DET-1 asserts byte-identical output for identical input with a supplied snapshot.
4. **`carried_candidates` rendering exposes a raw Layer2Assessment** beyond the qualitative proximity. *Mitigation:* the carried-candidates subsection reads only `katorthoma_proximity` (the qualitative level) + `considered_at` (the wrapper-supplied ISO). The `layer2_assessment` field's internals are not exposed in the rendering.
5. **The Character Kernel language overpromises or underpromises.** *Mitigation:* the R18A_CATEGORY_FRAMING constant uses language identical-in-substance to the J1 ADR's Character Kernel category text (adopted 2026-05-12 under D-SUBSTRATE-CATEGORY-CHARACTER-KERNEL-ADR-2026-05-12). The R18a-1 test asserts the presence of "Character Kernel" + the explicit "safety, ethics, or trustworthiness in any absolute sense" disclaimer.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for the kathekon-aligned alternative (step 5 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Seven sub-designs adopted as a parallel R18a-honest credential beside proximity:

- **A — Relationship to proximity.** Parallel credential alongside (not replacement, not composite). Proximity stays load-bearing for grade / authority / trajectory; kathekon gets its own credential field surfaced on the same record + payload but does NOT drive grade, authority, or trajectory.
- **B — Aggregation model.** `typical_kathekon_quality: KathekonQuality` — most-common-qualifying bucket across the window (`strong > moderate > marginal > contrary`), using `WindowConfig.typical_proximity_threshold` (no new threshold). Sibling `kathekon_quality_distribution: Record<KathekonQuality, number>` on `WindowSnapshot`, mirroring `proximity_distribution` and `deliberation_breadth_distribution`. Empty-window default `'contrary'` (conservative baseline; same shape as Decision A's `'intuited'` default).
- **C — Credential placement.** Add `typical_kathekon_quality` directly to `AccreditationRecord` + `AccreditationPayload`. No parallel `SenecanGradeId`. No new fifth progress dimension. The grade engine threads the new field through all three transition paths (no-transition / upgrade / downgrade) but does NOT consume it. Supabase `agent_accreditation` gains one column: `typical_kathekon_quality text not null default 'contrary'` (additive, idempotent, empty-table-safe — same pattern as Decision A's column). `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` automatically picks up the new field via payload projection — no parallel endpoint, no separate `kathekon_payload` (Q8 folded in).
- **D — Authority impact.** None. `authority_level` stays driven by `typical_proximity` via the existing `proximityToAuthority` mapping. The credential is observable on the record + payload but does not modulate operational permissions. Revisit condition deferred under PR7: evidence that consumers are interpreting the credential as an authority signal, or a feature requirement to gate authority on kathekon.
- **E — Layer 1 implications.** None. Raw signals (`is_kathekon` + `kathekon_quality`) already live on `EvaluatedAction` via the existing bridge; the aggregator gains one new computation using existing per-action data. `Layer1Schema` stays at v1 | v2 (per Decision B's items-1-3 bump). Rule A NOT engaged.
- **F — R18a category language.** No change. Character Kernel accommodates both proximity (HOW reasoned) and kathekon (WHETHER fitting) as observable reasoning patterns under the same umbrella. J1 ADR's revisit conditions are not triggered. No J2 ADR; no sub-category nomenclature.
- **G — Hand-back report surface.** Mirror Decision A's three-placement pattern. Section 1 per-decision kathekon notation is already in place from the hand-back build. Section 2 trajectory gains a `typical_kathekon_quality` headline + `kathekon_quality_distribution` line. Section 3 grade/authority/badge picks up the new field automatically from the `AccreditationPayload` projection — small addition to the existing `renderGradeSection(payload)` helper.

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the kathekon-aligned alternative build session (step 6 of the post-6b arc; `code-elevated` risk classification expected, paralleling the items 1–3 build's shape).

**Reasoning:** The substrate's Layer 2 assessment produces two parallel signals about each evaluated action. `katorthoma_proximity` measures HOW the agent reasoned (cognitive quality on the reflexive→sage_like ladder); `is_kathekon` + `kathekon_quality` measure WHETHER the act was the appropriate-in-the-circumstances fitting act. Both signals are Stoic-canonical and answer different questions. An agent might be high-proximity but consistently non-kathekon (highly considered acts that are nonetheless inappropriate in context) — or low-proximity but consistently kathekon (reflexive acts that nonetheless hit the mark). The proximity-only credential collapses these distinctions. This design recovers the kathekon signal as an additive parallel credential without rebasing the existing build. The structural pattern mirrors Decision A's `typical_deliberation_breadth` exactly — an additive aggregator computation + record/payload field + Supabase column + hand-back rendering — proving the pattern's reusability for additional R18a-honest observable credentials on the Character Kernel umbrella.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Built and Verified the seven design decisions (A–G) locked under `D-ATL-KATHEKON-ALIGNED-ALTERNATIVE-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` — the kathekon-aligned alternative as an additive parallel R18a-honest credential beside proximity, step 6 of 8 in the post-6b arc. Single-build proof per PR1: all seven decisions land in one session. The kathekon credential's structural pattern mirrors Decision A's `typical_deliberation_breadth` exactly — direct substitution of `KathekonQuality` for `DeliberationBreadth`, `typical_kathekon_quality` for `typical_deliberation_breadth`, `kathekon_quality_distribution` for `deliberation_breadth_distribution`, and `'contrary'` for `'intuited'` as the empty-window baseline.

**Reasoning:** The substrate's Layer 2 assessment already produces both proximity (HOW the agent reasoned) and kathekon (WHETHER the act was fitting) per-action. The items 1-3 build (Decision A) surfaced proximity-derived deliberation-breadth as a parallel observable credential, proving the pattern. This build applies the same pattern to the kathekon signal — recovering it as a load-bearing observable credential without rebasing the proximity-driven grade / authority / dimension / trajectory machinery. The seven decisions land additively: one new aggregator computation (two helpers), one new field on `WindowSnapshot` (two with the sibling distribution), one new field on `AccreditationRecord` + `AccreditationPayload`, one new Supabase column, threading through the grade-transition engine's three transition paths (field carriage only — no logic change), and two small line additions to the hand-back report renderer (Section 2 trajectory + Section 3 grade). Decisions A (parallel-not-replacement), D (no authority impact), E (no Layer 1 change), and F (no R18a category change) are framing decisions — they constrain what was NOT done; the build correctly preserved the proximity-driven machinery untouched. The four implementation-discretion picks at Step 1 (KathekonQuality alias re-declared inside trust-layer/; helpers in window-aggregator.ts alongside the deliberation-breadth pair; migration filename mirroring the existing one; test fixture extensions paralleling Decision A) were founder-confirmed in one batch and proceeded.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for the write-path into `agent_accreditation` (step 7 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Seven sub-designs adopted defining the surface that populates `agent_accreditation` rows by invoking the persistence layer's four async functions (which exist and are Verified, but are currently called by nothing):

- **A — Write-path surface.** Route + library. New library at `/website/src/lib/substrate/atl-accreditation-writer.ts` (filename build-session discretion) exposes the two entry points (per Decision D); new POST handler at `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` (or sibling file) calls the library. Both surfaces available: wrapper-internal consumers call the library directly; external callers go through the route. The library-only / route-only alternatives were rejected (library-only forces a re-architecture session when an HTTP surface becomes needed; route-only trips KG1 rule 1 — wrapper-internal consumers would self-call).
- **B — Write trigger.** Hybrid — explicit `seedAccreditation` / `updateAccreditation` call for the main row write; library automatically emits `appendInitialGradeHistory` on seed and `appendGradeHistory` on update *if and only if* `transitionResult.grade_changed === true`. Consumer decides *when* to persist; library decides *what audit entries to write*. On-every-`computeTrajectory`-call rejected (multiplies write volume); grade-transition-only rejected (row would drift); explicit-only rejected (audit trail too fragile under consumer discipline).
- **C — Auth model.** Agent_id-ownership check via signed token. **A10 (step 8) fills the seam** — A10 is the token-issuance + verification mechanism. Pre-A10 stopgap is one of three options chosen at the build session's design-decision gate: feature-flag gated (route returns 503 until env enabled); founder-only via service-role; founder-only via shared-secret. Build session records its election in its own decision-log entry. Shared-secret-as-long-term rejected (doesn't scale to multi-agent ownership); founder-only-as-long-term rejected (external use cases need non-founder callers).
- **D — Initial-seed vs trajectory-update separation.** Two entry points: `seedAccreditation(profile)` and `updateAccreditation(profile, transitionResult)`. Explicit; matches the persistence layer's existing function separation; impossible to misuse. Lookup-first rejected (extra read per write); consumer-driven flag rejected (footgun).
- **E — Atomicity.** Two awaited writes; not transactional. Upsert first, then history append. Failure between leaves state correct, history one entry behind — recoverable via retry (Decision F makes the retry safe). RPC transactional posture rejected as premature; history-first rejected (never-persisted failure mode harder to reason about).
- **F — Idempotency.** Idempotent upsert via the persistence layer's existing `onConflict: 'agent_id'` discipline. Duplicate history rows possible but acceptable (visible in audit trail; do not corrupt state). Client-provided idempotency key rejected (schema cost without proportional benefit); content-hashed idempotency rejected (over-engineered).
- **G — Observability.** Structured JSON logs per write to `console.log` (Vercel logs captures). Single helper emits one event per call with agent_id, call_type, actions_evaluated, senecan_grade, direction_of_travel, elapsed_ms, outcome, and grade-change fields when applicable. No schema change. Minimal-only rejected (lacks app-level context); AC10 provenance fields deferred under PR7 (schema cost without immediate need); webhook emission deferred (no real-time consumer use case yet).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the write-path build session. Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (Decision A's route + Decision C's auth surface engage AC7; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** After step 6, the substrate's R18a-honest credential surface carries three observable reasoning-pattern signals (`typical_proximity`, `typical_deliberation_breadth`, `typical_kathekon_quality`) — all defined in the type system and persistence-capable in Supabase. The persistence layer's four async functions exist and are tested. The public read endpoint is Live. But the table is empty: no code currently invokes the three write functions. The wrapper's `computeTrajectory` produces an advanced `CarriedProfile` with an updated `AccreditationRecord` on every call — but the wrapper is intentionally pure; it produces values, it does not persist. The write-path is the missing seam between the wrapper's pure computation and the persistence layer's awaited writes. Without it, the credential exists only in memory for the duration of one wrapper consumer's process. This design defines that seam. Decision A elects the surface (route + library); Decision B elects the trigger (hybrid — consumer decides cadence, library handles audit-trail bookkeeping); Decision C elects the auth model (A10-shaped token; A10 fills the seam next); Decision D elects the entry-point shape (two functions matching the persistence layer's separation); Decisions E + F + G elect the consistency, idempotency, and observability postures (two-awaited-writes; idempotent upsert; structured logs) — each chosen for simplicity at this stage with explicit revisit conditions if the failure modes prove load-bearing. The build session's risk is Critical because of the auth surface; the design's risk is Standard because no code lands.

## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Built the write-path into `agent_accreditation` per `D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` + `/adopted/atl-write-path-design.md` (step 7 of 8 in the post-6b arc). All seven design decisions A–G landed in a single Critical-risk build session (PR1 single-build proof). The persistence layer's three write functions (`upsertAccreditationRecord`, `appendGradeHistory`, `appendInitialGradeHistory`), Verified since 2026-05-15 but called by nothing, are now reachable via both a library (wrapper-internal consumers) and an HTTP POST handler (external callers).

**Step 1 elections (build-session discretion picks):**

- **Pre-A10 auth stopgap (load-bearing election):** option (1) **feature-flag gated** via `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` env var. Lowest blast radius pre-A10 — the surface exists in production code but is inert until the founder flips the flag. The auth-gate function signature (`verifyAgentIdOwnership(request, agent_id)`) is A10-shaped: post-A10 (step 8), the body swaps to per-agent token verification without changing the call site.
- **Library file path + name:** `/website/src/lib/substrate/atl-accreditation-writer.ts` (sibling to `atl-accreditation-store.ts` and `atl-wrapper.ts`). Matches the design doc's named target.
- **POST handler location:** added POST to the existing `/website/src/app/api/accreditation/[agent_id]/route.ts` alongside the GET. Next.js App Router supports both handlers in the same `route.ts`.
- **`buildGradeChangeEvent` export:** the function already exists as an exported function in `/website/src/lib/substrate/trust-layer/accreditation/accreditation-record.ts`. However, it requires a full `previous: AccreditationRecord` parameter and the `TransitionResult.trigger` does not carry all those fields (no `from_authority`). Per Decision D's discretion clause, `updateAccreditation` constructs the `GradeChangeEvent` inline from `transitionResult.trigger.from_grade` / `from_proximity` + `proximityToAuthority` (derived authority) + `transitionResult.record.actions_evaluated` (trigger_action_count) + `new Date().toISOString()` (timestamp).
- **Library test file structure:** new `/website/src/lib/substrate/__tests__/atl-accreditation-writer.test.ts` mirroring the existing `atl-accreditation-store.test.ts` plain-assertion harness pattern (PASS/FAIL labels, exit code 0/1, no Jest). The writer module's optional `deps` parameter (dependency-injection seam) lets tests mock the persistence layer + logger without invoking a real Supabase write.

**Reasoning:** After the design pass locked the seven decisions, the build session's job was to land code that implements them faithfully and that the founder can verify locally before deploying. The Critical classification is driven by Decision A's new POST surface + Decision C's new auth gate (AC7 engaged); the full Critical Change Protocol applied. The pre-A10 stopgap option (1) was elected for the smallest possible production-exposure delta: the surface lands, the route exists, but `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` remains UNSET in Vercel — every POST returns 503 "writes not yet enabled" until the founder explicitly flips the flag. The library is callable in-process by any wrapper-internal consumer (none exist yet), so the write-path is no longer architecturally dormant — it is operationally gated. A10 (step 8) replaces the env-flag gate with per-agent token verification, completing the auth seam Decision C named.

Public functions: `seedAccreditation(profile, deps?)` and `updateAccreditation(profile, transitionResult, deps?)`. The optional `deps` parameter (typed `AccreditationWriterDeps`) is the dependency-injection seam used by the test; production callers omit it and the default-deps object binds to the real persistence layer + `console.log` logger. No env change in Vercel this session — `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` is a NEW env var the route reads; pre-deploy default is UNSET (the route returns 503 until the founder explicitly sets it to the exact string `"true"`).

**Risk classification:** **Critical** under 0d-ii. AC7 ENGAGED (new auth surface — POST handler + `verifyAgentIdOwnership` gate). PR6 NOT engaged (no R20a / distress-classifier surface). Critical Change Protocol (0c-ii) ENGAGED — the seven CCP responses recorded below per the full template. The build-arc cache's "no current users" governing note applies to CCP step 3.

**Critical Change Protocol responses (per 0c-ii):**

1. **What is changing — plain language.** A new POST surface at `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` that writes credential rows to the `agent_accreditation` table via a new library (`atl-accreditation-writer.ts`). The library wraps the persistence layer's three already-Verified write functions. A new auth-gate function (pre-A10: env-flag-gated). A new structured-logging helper. New test files for both. The existing GET handler is byte-identical in behaviour after the edit (only its file-header comments + the `methodNotAllowed` helper's Allow header changed).

2. **What could break — specific failure modes.** Seven named risks: (a) auth-gate misconfiguration accepting unauthenticated writes (mitigated: strictest possible env-var check — only the exact string `"true"` enables writes; anything else fails closed); (b) auth-gate failure messages leaking internal details (mitigated: 503 message says "writes not yet enabled" without naming the env var; 401 message is the literal "Unauthorized." per Decision C's structural constraint); (c) hybrid trigger mis-routing the history function — calling `appendGradeHistory` when `grade_changed === false` (mitigated: UPDATE-2 test asserts no history call on no-change updates); (d) two-awaited-writes leaves state ahead of history (mitigated: this is the intended Decision E posture; structured logging makes the gap loud; idempotent retry recovers); (e) body-validation gaps producing 500 instead of 400 (mitigated: `validateWriteBody` does upfront shape checks on `kind` / `profile.agent_id` / `profile.accreditation_record` / `profile.regressing_check_count` / `transition_result.grade_changed` / `transition_result.record` before invoking the library); (f) existing GET handler regressing from co-located edits (mitigated: the existing route test still passes — its imports + assertions on OPTIONS + the 405 methods still work; the GET handler's behaviour is unchanged); (g) misconfigured env var at deploy producing unexpected behaviour (mitigated: the strictest-possible truthiness check + the default UNSET state → inert route).

3. **What happens to existing sessions.** **N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate** (per the build-arc cache's "no current users" governing note, affirmed 2026-05-10).

4. **Rollback plan.** Three paths: (A) **Before push:** `git reset --hard HEAD~1` discards the commit; no production effect. (B) **After push, before flipping the env var:** the route is inert in production (every POST returns 503 because the env var is UNSET); to remove the code, `git revert HEAD --no-edit` + push via GitHub Desktop. Vercel rebuilds (~2 min). Post-revert: the new library file gone; the POST handler removed from route.ts; the new response builders gone; the test files gone; the 405 method list restores POST. The orphaned `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` env var becomes inert (no code reads it). The GET handler is byte-identical to its pre-session state. ## 2026-05-16 — D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16

**Decision:** Locked the design for A10 — per-agent credentials (step 8 of 8 in the post-6b arc per the 2026-05-15 brainstorm sequencing). Nine sub-designs adopted defining the surface that replaces the write-path build's pre-A10 env-flag stopgap with per-agent token verification:

- **A — Token format.** Opaque random tokens (`sr_atl_<32 hex>`) with SHA-256 server-side lookup. Reuses the production `sr_live_<key>` pattern in `/website/src/lib/security.ts` (`hashKey` + `extractRawKey` + the lookup-and-verify flow). JWT, W3C VC, and hybrid rejected — the credential-format-third-parties-consume is the `AccreditationPayload` at the GET layer, not the auth token at the POST layer; F4 (AC10/AP2 alignment) lands at A12 via `credential_audit` provenance, not at the A10 token layer.
- **B — Issuance authority + agent_id binding.** Per-owner-account model. Each row carries `owner_user_id` (Supabase `auth.users.id`) + `agent_id`. Founder-only mint pre-launch; same shape supports self-service post-launch (a later-session change to the endpoint's authorisation logic, not a schema change). Open self-service rejected (squatting risk); founder-only-without-owner-binding rejected (forecloses self-service).
- **C — Credential storage.** Extend the existing `api_keys` table with `agent_id`, `owner_user_id`, `purpose`, `revoked_at` columns; add unique index `(owner_user_id, agent_id, purpose) WHERE purpose = 'atl_write'`; add lookup index `(purpose, agent_id) WHERE purpose = 'atl_write'`. `purpose` enum distinguishes existing `ecosystem` (sr_live keys) from new `atl_write` (sr_atl tokens). Greenfield `agent_credentials` table rejected on PR15 (re-implements production-proven `api_keys` plumbing); two-table separation rejected (duplicates behaviour).
- **D — Issuance flow + surface.** New admin endpoint `POST/DELETE /api/admin/accreditation-credentials`. Mirrors the existing `/api/admin/api-keys` pattern. Founder-only via Supabase auth + admin check (`ADMIN_USER_EMAIL` or `ADMIN_USER_ID` env var). Mint returns raw token once with explicit "shown once" warning. Sub-resource under public route group rejected (mixes admin into public surface); substrate-internal `/api/atl/` namespace rejected (no peer endpoints yet); out-of-band entirely rejected (forces a follow-on session).
- **E — Verification placement.** New `validateAtlWriteToken(rawToken, agent_id)` async function in `security.ts` alongside `validateApiKey`. Returns discriminated `AtlWriteValidationResult`. Route's `verifyAgentIdOwnership(request, agent_id)` becomes `async`; body rewritten to: (1) kill-switch check per Decision I, (2) `Authorization: Bearer sr_atl_<...>` header extract, (3) delegate to `validateAtlWriteToken`. Call site updates one `await`. Inside-route.ts rejected (too heavy post-A10); substrate-internal library rejected (auth logic is generic, not substrate-domain).
- **F — Revocation.** Reuse existing `is_active = false` + `suspended_reason` + add `revoked_at` timestamp column. Revocation via `DELETE` handler. No reactivation in this build (deferred under PR7). Separate `revoked_credentials` table rejected (duplicates `is_active`); no-revocation rejected (untenable without short expiry).
- **G — Rotation + expiry.** No expiry; only revocation. Matches existing `api_keys` precedent. Renewal = revoke-and-reissue. No `expires_at` column. Per-credential `expires_at` deferred under PR7; refresh-token flow rejected (heavy for server-to-server credentials with no browser exposure).
- **H — Audit trail + observability.** Asymmetric: Vercel structured logs (`atl_verify` event JSON, mirroring write-path's `atl_write` pattern) for verification path; new `credential_audit` Supabase table for issuance + revocation events (`event_type`, `credential_id`, `actor_user_id`, `agent_id`, `details jsonb`, `created_at`). The asymmetric rates (verification high-frequency; issuance/revocation rare-but-forensically-important) drive the split. Verification-to-logs-only rejected (Vercel 30-day retention loses long-tail forensic trails); all-to-table rejected (verification volumes would balloon table).
- **I — Pre-A10 stopgap retirement.** Keep `SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` as a kill-switch. Env-flag check stays at the top of `verifyAgentIdOwnership`. Semantics shift: pre-A10 = "is the write surface enabled at all"; post-A10 = "if unset, override A10 and block all writes globally". 2-min phone-flip emergency lockdown capability. Remove entirely rejected (loses defence-in-depth at near-zero cost); staged-rollout mechanism rejected (over-architected).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the A10 build session. Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (the auth-gate swap engages AC7 + R17; new admin endpoint engages AC7; schema additions engage AC7; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** After step 7 (write-path build), the substrate's POST surface at `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` is inert by default (`SUBSTRATE_WRITE_PATH_ENABLED` UNSET → every POST returns 503). The pre-A10 stopgap is coarse-grained (set the flag → any caller can write any row; unset → no one can write any row); appropriate for the build phase but not the long-term auth model. Decision C of the write-path design named A10 as the eventual filler. This design specifies the *how*: nine decisions covering token format, issuance binding, storage, issuance flow, verification placement, revocation, rotation, audit, and stopgap retirement. The load-bearing choice is Decision A's opaque-token format, which cascades into Decision C's "extend `api_keys`" path (maximum reuse of production-tested infrastructure: SHA-256 hashing + atomic usage RPC + suspension mechanics + Stripe linkage + admin endpoint pattern). The build session is much lighter than a greenfield approach would be. PR15 operational discipline is the dominant influence on the design: the existing `api_keys` + `validateApiKey` infrastructure is the production-adjacent reusable primitive being reused.

## 2026-05-17 — D-BILLING-MODEL-LOCKED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Locked the Option D billing model design — per-loop base rate ($0.02) + LLM-token-cost overage (50% of base trigger; ×2 multiplier) — replacing the current per-API-call (count-based) model. Eight sub-designs adopted defining Option D's surface (session #1 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail per the predecessor close's Part 2):

- **A — Loop definition.** One loop = one wrapper invocation, identified by `(api_key_id, loop_id)` with `loop_id` as a UUIDv4 propagated via `X-Loop-Id` request header (server auto-generates if absent). Cascades into Decision E (cost-tracking surface keys off `loop_id`). REJECTED: `CarriedProfile` lifecycle (ties to inert write surface); single `/api/reason` call (mis-attributes wrappers); caller-asserted-only (trust gap without server-side fallback).
- **B — Base rate per loop.** $0.02, uniform across surfaces; stored as `LOOP_BASE_RATE_CENTS = 2` in `/website/src/lib/stripe.ts`. ~4x R5 ratio on typical loops; comfortable headroom; presentable as "two cents per task". Re-tunable pre-Stripe based on first-2–4-weeks real-cost distribution (Elevated edit). REJECTED: $0.01 (no R5 headroom; constant overage noise); $0.05 (presentation risk; 20x current per-call rate); tiered by surface (violates "the unit makes sense").
- **C — Overage trigger threshold.** Overage fires when loop's Anthropic cost > 50% of base rate (`OVERAGE_TRIGGER_RATIO = 0.5`). Self-balancing if Anthropic prices shift — multiplier stays put. REJECTED: fixed token count (varies with model mix; couples to current Anthropic pricing); fixed USD cost (needs re-tuning at every Anthropic price change).
- **D — Overage rate.** Anthropic cost above threshold × 2 (`OVERAGE_RATE_MULTIPLIER = 2.0`); R5's 2x ratio satisfied at the loop level by construction. REJECTED: ×2.5 fixed (double-charges for overhead the base rate already covered; presentation risk); tiered multiplier (rent-seeking pattern; complexity).
- **E — Cost tracking surface.** Both — extend `api_key_usage` with five loop-level columns (`loop_count`, `anthropic_cost_cents`, `billed_cents`, `overage_count`, `overage_cents`) for aggregate quota path AND new `loop_billing_events` append-only ledger for forensic granularity. New `/website/src/lib/loop-cost-tracker.ts` module (sibling to `r20a-cost-tracker.ts`) covers Haiku + Sonnet per-model pricing. The `increment_api_usage` RPC extends to also write a `loop_billing_events` row transactionally. REJECTED: `api_key_usage`-only (loses forensic detail); `loop_billing_events`-only (breaks fast-quota path).
- **F — Migration path.** Full cutover — new `billing_model` column on `api_keys` with CHECK constraint `(per_call, per_loop)`; all existing rows default to `per_loop`; per-call rate config retires; existing `monthly_limit`/`daily_limit`/`max_chain_iterations` retained as anti-abuse caps over loops. The "no current users" governing note (build-arc cache 2026-05-10) is load-bearing — no third-party customers to coordinate with. STATUS-REVENUE-MODEL.md Tasks 4+5 marked Superseded at build session. REJECTED: grandfathering (moot); flag-day mandatory (no customers); opt-in V2 (over-engineers for non-state).
- **G — R5 enforcement transition.** Keep `cost_health_snapshots` as retrospective sanity check on the prospective formula; R5 manifest text unchanged. Defence-in-depth; the existing text already accommodates both interpretations. The cost-health alert becomes an *exception* signal post-launch (a fire = formula bug or accounting error, not a normal-state signal). REJECTED: replace retrospective entirely (loses independent verification); rewrite R5 manifest (Elevated cache-update work unnecessary).
- **H — Communication surface.** Both — response headers (`X-Loop-Id`, `X-Loop-Cost-Cents`, `X-Anthropic-Cost-Cents`, `X-Overage-Fired`, `X-Overage-Cents`, `X-Loop-Internal-Calls`) on every `/api/reason` and `/api/score-iterate` response under per-loop billing AND Stripe webhook + monthly invoice rendering reading from `loop_billing_events`. Addresses fair-license criteria "the meter is visible", "usage data exports cleanly", "cost-aware agents". REJECTED: response-headers-only (no canonical billing surface); invoices-only (the meter is hidden — rent-seeking pattern the essay warns against).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the build spec for the Option D build session (session #2 of the new post-6b arc tail). Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (schema migrations affecting `api_keys` + `api_key_usage`; new `loop_billing_events` ledger; Stripe webhook integration; response-header emission on the loop-producing surfaces; engages AC7 via deployment-config + access-control changes; full Critical Change Protocol applies).

**Reasoning:** The current per-API-call billing model has two structural flaws (per the 2026-05-16 brainstorm in the predecessor close's Part 2): (i) the founder absorbs LLM-cost variance — a 5-iteration loop costs the same to bill as a 1-iteration loop but consumes 5x the Anthropic tokens; R5's 2x ratio is enforced retrospectively via `cost_health_snapshots` alerts not built into the pricing formula; (ii) the billed unit (API call) doesn't match the value unit (the agent's loop). Option D addresses both with a per-loop base rate that covers ~80% of usage at a 4x R5 ratio and an Anthropic-cost-relative overage that fires only on heavy deliberation chains where the customer caused the variance. The PR15 dominant influence — the existing `api_key_usage` + `cost_health_snapshots` + `r20a-cost-tracker.ts` + Stripe billing infrastructure is the production-adjacent reusable primitive — kept the build-session surgery to a minimum: extend rather than replace. The fair-license criteria from the Nate B Jones essay are the external benchmark every decision was checked against ("the meter is visible and the unit makes sense"; "failed or low-value work isn't billed identically to completed work"; "the buyer can set caps" — deferred under PR7 with revisit condition; "usage data exports cleanly"; "the rate card holds for the term without quiet changes after adoption" — adopted as the post-launch policy).

- **Real-cost-distribution-based base-rate re-tuning.** First 2–4 weeks of live operation produce per-loop cost distributions; the base rate may be re-tuned. Revisit condition: 2 weeks post Option D build deploy + Stripe activation. Re-tuning is Elevated under 0d-ii.

- **Grandfathering policy.** When real customers exist, model changes follow contracted-renewal rules (fair-license criterion). Revisit condition: first paying customer signed.
- **R5 manifest amendment to formalise prospective/retrospective split.** Revisit condition: real operational experience shows the manifest text needs disambiguation OR a future formula change creates ambiguity.
- **`cost_health_snapshots` schema extension.** Could add `prospective_ratio_at_period_end`. Revisit condition: a divergence between prospective and retrospective observed.
- **Alert escalation paths.** Sage Ops integration; SMS notification. Revisit condition: customer-facing operations require it.
- **Webhook emission on overage-fired events.** Revisit condition: customer requests it OR billing-anomaly use case surfaces.
- **Budget-cap enforcement.** When customer's monthly bill crosses threshold, future loops 429. Revisit condition: enterprise customer requests it.
- **OpenTelemetry trace fields in response headers.** Revisit condition: A12 scheduled.
- **GraphQL / JSON-RPC billing query surface.** Programmatic access. Revisit condition: customer use case.

## 2026-05-17 — D-BILLING-MODEL-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Built the Option D per-loop billing model per `D-BILLING-MODEL-LOCKED-2026-05-17` + `/adopted/billing-model-design.md` (session #2 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail). All 17 expected file changes from the design's build-session implementation summary table landed in a single Critical-risk session (PR1 single-build proof). The metering layer is wired across `/api/reason` + `/api/score-iterate`; the new `loop_billing_events` ledger persists per-loop bills via the extended `increment_api_usage` RPC; the six X-Loop-* response headers emit on every billable response branch; Stripe webhook handler `invoice.created` attaches per-day-aggregate line items (inert until `STRIPE_PER_LOOP_PRICE_ID` is set in a follow-on session per Step 0 election).

**Step 1 elections (build-session discretion picks):**

- **(a) CORS Access-Control-Expose-Headers:** option (i) **defer browser exposure under PR7** — server-to-server callers (curl, server-side wrappers) see X-Loop-* headers via direct response inspection; browser-side wrappers don't until a follow-on session adds the six headers to the CORS expose block. Acceptable for the pre-launch period (no browser callers yet).
- **(b) Invoice line-item shape:** option **per-day-aggregate** — Stripe webhook attaches one Invoice Item per day of usage, with `metadata.loops_count` showing the loops aggregated. CSV download (per-loop forensic granularity at the invoice surface) deferred under PR7 — Decision H's "usage data exports cleanly" criterion satisfied by `loop_billing_events` Supabase query access; CSV adds accounting convenience.
- **(c) Dead per-call code paths:** option **retain for one release cycle** — the existing per-call counters on `api_key_usage` (`total_calls`, `guardrail_calls`, etc.) continue to increment alongside the new `loop_count` aggregate. Rollback safety. A follow-on Standard-risk session removes them after 2 weeks of stable Option D operation.
- **(d) Test file structure:** option **sibling** — `/website/src/lib/__tests__/loop-cost-tracker.test.ts` matches the `r20a-cost-tracker` pattern; metering layer tested independently of route integration. 76 tests landed; 76 pass; tsc clean.
- **(e — NEW) Multi-HTTP-request loops with shared X-Loop-Id:** option **hard error on duplicate** — the `loop_billing_events` UNIQUE (api_key_id, loop_id) constraint is enforced; second insert returns HTTP 400 `loop_id_already_billed`. Wrappers learn to issue fresh loop_ids per HTTP request. Multi-HTTP-request loops with shared loop_id stay explicitly deferred under Decision A's PR7. Surfaced this election (5th — not in the original prompt) from Part A route reads where the UNIQUE constraint vs "terminal call" framing produced ambiguity.

**Step 0 elections:**

- **Stripe Price ID:** **deferred to a follow-on session** — the metering layer + webhook handler land in this build; the live invoice flow waits until you generate the Price ID in the Stripe Dashboard and set `STRIPE_PER_LOOP_PRICE_ID` in Vercel. Metering and ledger persistence are fully operational without the Price ID; only `invoice.created` rendering is inert.
- **Session split:** **natural pause at Step 8** offered but not taken — you elected to push through Steps 9–14 in one session.

**Reasoning:** The design pass (predecessor session) locked the eight decisions A–H; the build session's job was to land code faithful to the spec without scope creep. Five build-session discretion picks (Step 1) plus the Stripe Price ID timing (Step 0) gave you the surface-level controls without dragging design decisions into the build. The single-build proof discipline (PR1) means all 17 changes ship together — schema, RPC, module, Stripe constants, R20a integration, route wiring on both surfaces, webhook, discovery files, STATUS supersession, tests — so the rollback path is one git revert + one SQL paste-block. The Critical-risk classification is driven by Decision E's RPC + schema changes (AC7 engaged via deployment-config + access-control changes) and the integration into both R20a-perimeter-adjacent routes; PR6 not engaged because the R20a classifier surface itself is not touched (only the optional `loop_id` param on `logClassifierRun` and the corresponding `classifier_cost_log.loop_id` column — both additive, both non-functional changes to the classifier path). The "no current users" governing note made the Critical Change Protocol's step 3 moot.

**Critical Change Protocol responses (per 0c-ii):**

1. **What is changing — plain language.** Per-API-call billing replaced by per-loop billing for paid API-key callers. One loop = one wrapper invocation (one HTTP request to `/api/reason` or `/api/score-iterate`). Every loop costs $0.02 base; if the loop's Anthropic-token cost exceeds 50% of base ($0.01), an overage of 2× the excess is added — so customers pay for the LLM cost variance they cause, and R5's 2× revenue/cost floor holds by construction. New `loop_billing_events` ledger; 5 new aggregate columns on `api_key_usage`; new `billing_model` column on `api_keys` (all existing rows defaulted to `per_loop`); extended `increment_api_usage` RPC (backward-compatible — new params have DEFAULTs); new `loop-cost-tracker.ts` module; integration into both loop-producing routes with six new X-Loop-* response headers per Decision H; Stripe webhook `invoice.created` handler (inert until Price ID set).

2. **What could break — seven specific failure modes.** (a) Metering mis-attributes cost between loops — mitigated by KG1 rule 4 per-request scope + ACC-8 test + UNIQUE constraint. (b) computeLoopBill arithmetic errors — mitigated by BILL-1 through BILL-7 tests covering Decision D's worked examples + R5 floor at scale. (c) Transactional RPC fails between aggregate + ledger writes — mitigated by single PL/pgSQL function (one implicit transaction). (d) Response headers leak internal state — mitigated by explicit Decision-H naming + HDR-1 through HDR-4 tests; no model identifiers or raw tokens in headers. (e) Stripe webhook mis-renders line items — mitigated by inert posture (Price ID unset per Step 0). (f) Dead per-call code paths become live — mitigated by Decision F full cutover (all rows default to per_loop). (g) Schema migration fails partway — mitigated by IF NOT EXISTS idempotency throughout.

3. **What happens to existing sessions.** **N/A — only founder + test logins exist; no third-party sessions to invalidate** (per the build-arc cache's "no current users" governing note, affirmed 2026-05-10).
