## 2026-05-17 — D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Locked the pass-through fields design — six enterprise-accountability fields landing on `EvaluatedAction` and `CarriedProfile` as optional pass-through metadata (session #3 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail per the predecessor close's Next Session Should). Six sub-designs adopted defining the substrate's enterprise-readability surface; the substrate validates the enum values and persists them but does not interpret them for Layer 1/2/3 reasoning.

- **A — operation_class.** 9-value enum from the prompt kit (`read`, `search`, `summarize`, `draft`, `recommend`, `write`, `approve`, `execute`, `delete`) + `unknown` default. Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Soft-fallback on unrecognised values lands them in `unknown` with warning log. Cascades into Option C tiered-per-action billing (deferred under PR7 — `operation_class` is the gating field; once populated, Option C becomes implementable). REJECTED: 3-value trichotomy (loses SEARCH/APPROVE/DELETE distinctions); 5-value middle-ground (invents non-source taxonomy); free-form string (fails "the unit makes sense").
- **B — downstream_identity_model.** 7-value enum from the prompt kit (`delegated_user`, `service_account`, `vendor_framework`, `api_key`, `browser_session`, `mcp_server`, `unknown`) + `unknown` default. Optional on `CarriedProfile`. Carries accountability-attribution signal procurement reviews ask about. REJECTED: 4-value coarser (loses api_key/browser_session/mcp_server distinctions); free-form (no aggregation).
- **C — path_posture.** 4-value enum from the prompt kit (`endorsed`, `open_api`, `ambiguous`, `unsanctioned`) + `ambiguous` default (matches the prompt-kit-canonical honest middle). Optional on `CarriedProfile`. Carries the 🟢🟡🔴 access-path flag procurement reviews use. Substrate does not enforce; wrappers self-report. REJECTED: 3-value drop-ambiguous (forces false confidence); boolean (loses unsanctioned vs open_api semantic).
- **D — target_system.** Two-field shape: `target_system_vendor` (10-value enum — `salesforce`, `microsoft`, `servicenow`, `sap`, `workday`, `zendesk`, `hubspot`, `atlassian`, `other`, `none`; default `none`) + `target_system_detail` (optional free-form string; 100-char length cap; no default). Both optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Vendor enum enables aggregation; detail captures sub-system granularity (e.g., `salesforce` + `opportunities`). REJECTED: single vendor enum (loses sub-system detail); free-form string only (no aggregation); hierarchical `vendor.subsystem` (convention-by-documentation; harder to validate).
- **E — outcome_verification.** 4-value enum including external_auditor (`self_reported`, `system_confirmed`, `external_auditor`, `not_applicable`) + `self_reported` default (most-honest baseline). Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Forward-looking external_auditor included for future audit/attestation use cases. REJECTED: 3-value drop-external_auditor (forecloses third-party verification cases); boolean (loses self_reported vs system_confirmed vs external_auditor trust semantics).
- **F — reversibility_signal.** 4-value enum (`reversible`, `partially_reversible`, `irreversible`, `unknown`) + `unknown` default (matches Q3 `ambiguous` pattern — encourages honest "I don't know"). Optional on `EvaluatedAction`. Downstream risk classification can weight `unknown` + `execute` + `irreversible-by-default-assumption` as high-risk. REJECTED: 3-value with `irreversible` default (over-cautious; forces false confidence); boolean (loses partially_reversible bucket).

## 2026-05-17 — D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Implement the six pass-through fields per `D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17`. Six enum types (`OperationClass`, `DownstreamIdentityModel`, `PathPosture`, `TargetSystemVendor`, `OutcomeVerification`, `ReversibilitySignal`) and five fields on `EvaluatedAction` (operation_class, target_system_vendor, target_system_detail, outcome_verification, reversibility_signal) land in `evaluation.ts`. Two fields on `CarriedProfile` (downstream_identity_model, path_posture) land in `atl-wrapper.ts` per the build-session discretion call (Step 0). A new validator module + 80-test suite land at `trust-layer/validation/`. Three discovery files document the seven fields with consistent language.

**Reasoning:** Executes the design adopted yesterday at `D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-LOCKED-2026-05-17`. All six decisions A–F implemented as written (Step 0 founder election: "Implement as written"). Backward-compatible per-field optional posture preserves existing substrate consumers (ATL Wrapper, kathekon-aligned scorer, hand-back report) — every field defaults to a sensible value; reading a field that was never populated returns the documented default. The substrate validates and persists; it does NOT interpret these fields for Layer 1/2/3 reasoning. PR15 bespoke election justified — substrate-internal type-system + validator code has no Anthropic primitive substitute; `mcp-builder` skill is the closest forward pointer (R18c-relevant for post-launch MCP tool description exposure) but does not address substrate-internal type validation.

This preserves the boundary; no new file introduced.

## 2026-05-17 — D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17

**Decision:** Rewrite the A10 per-agent-credentials design (`/adopted/atl-a10-design.md`) in full to integrate three things that changed since `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` was adopted. **Supersedes** `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-2026-05-16` (predecessor entry's Status amended to `Superseded by D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17` in the same operation). Session #5 of 6 in the new post-6b arc tail (governance — design pass only; no code lands; A10 build at session #6 implements the rewrite). Three sub-decisions adopted:

- **Decision 1 — owner_user_id + agent_id correction (Finding 1).** The original Decision C said "Extend `api_keys` with `agent_id`, `owner_user_id`, `purpose`, `revoked_at` columns." Production schema at `/api/api-keys-schema.sql` lines 75 + 77 + 105 confirms the first two columns + the lookup index already exist; the original design's `owner_user_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)` was wrong (production references `public.profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`). Elected: (b) Keep `public.profiles(id)` reference target; add Postgres CHECK constraint `CHECK (purpose != 'atl_write' OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))` to enforce the load-bearing NOT NULL invariant at the schema level. REJECTED: (a) application-level enforcement only (single-code-path defence; PR7-deferred CHECK as defence-in-depth needed later anyway); (c) migrate to `auth.users(id)` (drops + recreates FK on live table; Elevated risk for no operational gain; profiles is downstream of auth.users so functionally equivalent). Migration narrows: only `purpose` + `revoked_at` are NEW columns on `api_keys`; `agent_id` + `owner_user_id` are reused; existing `idx_api_keys_owner_user_id` reused.

- **Decision 2 — loop_billing_events integration.** Option D went Live on 2026-05-17 (`D-BILLING-MODEL-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17`). Elected: (a) **No direct integration.** Credential lifecycle events (issuance, revocation) stay in `credential_audit` only (per Decision H). The write-path POST `/api/accreditation/[agent_id]` is NOT separately metered — the wrapper's triggering `/api/reason` call already emitted the `loop_billing_events` row; the POST is a downstream effect (separate billing would double-bill the same logical loop). The build session adds a nullable `loop_id UUID` column to `agent_accreditation` for downstream JOIN-based forensic traceability ("which loop triggered this accreditation update?"). REJECTED: (b) light integration with `'credential_write'` surface enum value (mild semantic pollution; no operational gain); (c) full integration with three new surface enum values + admin-fee policy decisions (heavy; duplicates credential_audit; pollutes surface enum with three non-LLM values).

- **Decision 3 — pass-through fields integration (three sub-decisions).** Seven fields landed in the substrate type system on 2026-05-17 (`D-PASS-THROUGH-FIELDS-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-17`). Sub-decisions:
  - **3a — Per-credential scoping** (the 2 `CarriedProfile` fields: `downstream_identity_model`, `path_posture`). Elected: (b) **Nullable scoping columns on `api_keys`** (`scope_downstream_identity_model`, `scope_path_posture`) for `purpose='atl_write'` rows. NULL = no restriction; specific value = the credential only matches CarriedProfiles with that exact value. Enforcement at verification time via `validateAtlWriteToken`'s extended signature (now accepts optional CarriedProfile param; new `'wrong_scope'` failure reason). Admin endpoint accepts optional scope params on mint. REJECTED: (a) required scoping (overkill pre-launch); (d) no scoping at all (forecloses the use case the pass-through fields design specifically named as session #5 work).
  - **3b — AccreditationPayload typical-class exposure** (the 4 `EvaluatedAction`-derived aggregates: `typical_operation_class`, `typical_target_system_vendor`, `typical_outcome_verification`, `typical_reversibility_signal`). Elected: (a) **All four typical_* fields exposed.** Matches the existing pattern (`buildAccreditationPayload` already exposes `typical_deliberation_breadth` + `typical_kathekon_quality`). Procurement reviewers reading `AccreditationPayload` see the agent's typical operational profile per the prompt-kit's Agent System Touch Map output. REJECTED: (b) partial — only `typical_operation_class` (no significant cost savings; loses 3 of 4 fields' procurement value); (c) defer to a later session (forces a second schema migration on `agent_accreditation`).
  - **3c — Persistence shape.** Elected: (a) **Aggregates only — typical_* fields persist on `agent_accreditation`** as additive nullable columns. Matches the existing wrapper-computes-aggregates-then-POSTs pattern (`typical_deliberation_breadth` + `typical_kathekon_quality` already work this way). Raw `EvaluatedAction` history is NOT persisted (deferred under PR7 — a new `evaluated_action_history` table is the natural shape if forensic queries beyond typical_* become a real use case). REJECTED: (b) aggregates + raw history on a new table (heavier build; forensic use case not yet present); (c) in-memory only (inconsistent with 3b=(a) — cannot expose what isn't persisted).

No code, schema, env, or production exposure this session — these decisions are the rewritten build spec for the A10 build session (session #6 of the new post-6b arc tail). Expected risk classification for the build session: **Critical** under 0d-ii (full Critical Change Protocol applies; auth surface change + schema additions to `api_keys` + new `credential_audit` table + extensions to `agent_accreditation`).

**Reasoning:** Three things changed since the original A10 design was adopted on 2026-05-16: (1) the 2026-05-16 post-session brainstorm surfaced Finding 1 — `owner_user_id` + `agent_id` already exist on `api_keys` in production, AND the reference target was wrong (`public.profiles(id)` not `auth.users(id)`); (2) Option D went Live with `loop_billing_events` as the metering ledger, creating an integration question for A10's credential surface; (3) seven pass-through fields landed in the substrate type system, and per the pass-through fields design's §Integration §A10 section, the A10 rewrite is where the per-credential scoping + AccreditationPayload typical-class exposure decisions get made. The rewrite consolidates all three into one canonical spec (per Step 0 election: rewrite-in-full not addendum) — fewer files for the A10 build session at #6 to read. Decision 1's CHECK-constraint election aligns with the A10 build's Critical-risk posture (defence-in-depth at near-zero cost; additive idempotent migration); Decision 2's no-integration posture keeps Option D's meter focused on LLM-mediated loops without double-billing; Decision 3's nullable-scoping + all-four-typical_* + aggregates-only matches the existing patterns the substrate already uses and minimises build session #6's surgery scope.

## 2026-05-21 — D-ATL-A10-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-21

**Decision:** Implemented the rewritten A10 per-agent-credentials design (`/adopted/atl-a10-design.md`, `D-ATL-A10-DESIGN-LOCKED-REWRITE-2026-05-17`) in full — all nine decisions A–I + the three rewrite integrations. The substrate write surface (`POST /api/accreditation/[agent_id]`) is now gated by per-agent opaque `sr_atl_` tokens bound to a specific `agent_id` (+ optional per-credential scope on `downstream_identity_model` / `path_posture`), minted/revoked through a new founder-only admin endpoint, audited in a new `credential_audit` table; `AccreditationPayload` exposes four new `typical_*` aggregates; `agent_accreditation` gains a nullable `loop_id` JOIN-trace column; `agent-card.json` declares the A10 auth method for A2A discovery. **Closes the post-6b arc.** Code complete + in-session-Verified (tsc clean; all unit + regression tests green); production deploy + smoke-test Verification is the founder's between-sessions step (per the Critical Change Protocol step 5 + the close's Founder Verification block — same posture as the write-path build).

**Reasoning:** Final sub-session (#6 of 6) of the post-6b arc tail. Per the design's PR15 election, the existing `api_keys` + `validateApiKey` opaque-token infrastructure IS the production-adjacent primitive A10 extends (Finding 1: the `agent_id` + `owner_user_id` columns already exist, referencing `public.profiles(id)`), so the migration is additive and narrow rather than a greenfield credential table. Four founder Step-1 elections (AskUserQuestion): (1) migrations run in Supabase SQL Editor; (2) **port-mirror reconciled in this build**; (3) **immediate orphaned-credential auto-revocation built now**; (4) **admin check reuses the existing `ADMIN_USER_ID` env var** (no new env var).

**Refinements to the locked design (build-session discretion, within the design's granted latitude):**
- **CHECK-constraint exemption for revoked rows (forced by election 3).** The locked CHECK `(purpose != 'atl_write' OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))` is incompatible with immediate orphan auto-revocation: `ON DELETE SET NULL` on `owner_user_id` would violate it for an active atl_write row, blocking the profile deletion. Refined to `(purpose != 'atl_write' OR is_active = false OR (agent_id IS NOT NULL AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL))`. The load-bearing invariant (ACTIVE atl_write credentials are owner+agent-bound) is preserved exactly; revoked tombstones are exempt; a revoked credential can never authenticate (verification filters `is_active = true`). A `BEFORE DELETE ON public.profiles` trigger (`revoke_atl_credentials_on_profile_delete`) revokes the credential first, then the FK-nulling succeeds. Founder accepted by running the SQL.
- **Pure-function factoring for testability (PR2).** `evaluateAtlWriteRow` (pure decision) factored out of `validateAtlWriteToken`; `extractCarriedProfileForAuth` + `extractWriteExtras` factored into `request-helpers.ts`; `validateMintInput` factored into the admin endpoint's `validation.ts`. The Supabase round-trips (admin mint/revoke, route auth-gate end-to-end) are verified by the founder's post-deploy smoke tests — identical posture to `D-ATL-WRITE-PATH-BUILD-WIRED-VERIFIED-2026-05-16`.
- **Port-mirror scope (election 2).** The source-of-truth `/trust-layer/` accreditation files were drifted further than the A10 fields implied (also missing the May-16 `deliberation_breadth` + `kathekon_quality` fields). Reconciliation was bounded to the two named accreditation files (`/trust-layer/types/accreditation.ts` + `/trust-layer/accreditation/accreditation-record.ts`), adding all six fields + the six enum types inline (matching that tree's self-contained convention); the unrelated full `evaluation.ts` re-port (EvaluatedAction / WindowSnapshot drift) was left out of scope. These files are reference-only (outside the compiled tree) — zero deploy impact.

Post-push: `git revert <sha> && git push` → Vercel rebuilds to the pre-endpoint shape (route 404/absent). `discovery_sessions` rows are hard-deletable (R17h: `deleteSession`/`deleteAgentSessions`). The engine/store/Stage-1 table remain inert on rollback — this stage is purely additive. ## 2026-05-22 — D-SAGE-REFLECT-STAGE-B-METERING-FIX-AND-LIVE-VERIFICATION-2026-05-22

**Decision:** Fixed two metering defects in the Stage-B endpoint surfaced by the live smoke test, then completed the founder live-verification (Critical Change Protocol step 5) against production with `SAGE_REFLECT_ENABLED=true`. **Sage Reflect is now Live / Verified (gated)** — the fourth Sage Practice product; the Calling → Reasoning → Assent → Reflect loop is closed.

**The defects (both AI-introduced; found via the post-deploy log line added this session):** the answer path returned 503 `metering failed` because `increment_api_usage` rejected a non-integer: `invalid input syntax for type integer: "1.02"`. Root cause (Diagnostic-certain): (1) the per-call Sonnet cost was passed to `recordLoopBilling` as a raw float — the RPC stores INTEGER cents, and the loop-cost-tracker convention is "rounding to integer cents happens at the billing-construction step"; the route now rounds (`Math.round`) at the meter boundary, recording sub-cent Layer-1 costs as 0 (base-rate loop, the Sage Calling posture) while still flagging `internalCalls`/`modelsUsed` when a call occurred. (2) `usageToCents` divided microcents by 1000; 1 cent = 10,000 microcents, so the figure was 10× inflated — corrected to `/10000` (matches the canonical `(tokens/1e6)·USD_per_million·100`). The Sonnet extraction itself was always succeeding (the `1.02` was a real computed cost); only the billing write failed. Two earlier same-session fixes also landed on the answer path: a static `decryptPersistedState` import (removed a fragile dynamic `import()`), and the server-error log line that made this diagnosis possible. Regression locked: `reflect-service.test.ts` COST-1..4 (magnitude `/10000`; sub-cent; integer-roundable; zero-usage→0).

**Live verification (founder-run, production, `agent_reflect_smoke_v1` unscoped `sr_atl_` credential):** auth — no token / bad token / valid+wrong-agent → **401**, valid+matching → **200**. Full walk on real Sonnet calls: Q1→Q2→Q3→**FD-R1 verification step**→Q4→Q5→Q6→**complete**, `exit_path:'sage_reasoning'` (RS-1). FD-R3 fired live (the canned smoke answer's bare pressure-assent denial → `profile_update_confidence:'low'` + a `pressure_assent` scrutiny flag). Completion surfaced the Sage Assent profile read-back (grade `pre_progress`; per-domain `katorthoma_proximity_by_domain`; dimension levels; `direction_of_travel`), the developer note, and the R19d mandatory mirror note. Harm-flagged open → `status:'flagged'`, the Zone-3 developer note, no reflection (R20a/SR-9). Every Stage-B surface confirmed live: auth, kill switch, translation-sandwich (Sonnet Q1–Q4), deterministic engine, FD-R1 + FD-R3, Sage Assent feed, SR-15 per-domain proximity, mirror principle, Zone-3 boundary, metering.

**Files touched:**
- `website/src/app/api/practice/reflect/route.ts` — `makeMeter` rounds to integer cents; added the server-error log line (observability).
- `website/src/lib/sage-reflect/reflect-extractor.ts` — `usageToCents` microcents→cents `/10000`.
- `website/src/lib/sage-reflect/reflect-service.ts` — static `decryptPersistedState` import (removed dynamic `import()`).
- `website/src/lib/sage-reflect/__tests__/reflect-service.test.ts` — COST-1..4 regression (suite now 20/0).
- `smoke-test-reflect.sh` (repo-root local helper) — fixed sections 1–3 quoting; adaptive Q-walk.

**Risk classification:** **Critical** (changes to the live authenticated endpoint's metering path; AC7 surface). But strictly repairs an already-503ing path; behaviour-preserving for auth/flag/safety. Verified: `tsc` clean; 8 suites green (Stage A 115/0 + Stage B 52/0 — reflect-service now 20/0); live smoke test passed end-to-end.

**Rollback path:** unset `SAGE_REFLECT_ENABLED` → all calls 503, no redeploy; or `git revert` the metering-fix commit → the answer path returns to its prior (broken) 503, no other surface affected.

Sage Calling Live (gated); substrate A7 Verified; A10 Live + Verified; Layer-3 + R20a substrate gates UNSET. Build-arc "no current users" still holds (founder + test logins only).

**Decision:** Built the full Sage Reflect A-track (Steps 0–3) per `/drafts/2026-05-23-track-followons-design-pack.md` §A. **A3(a)** (Standard, governance): SR-9 of `/adopted/sage-reflect-product-design.md` now states the canonical harm-flag carrier explicitly — the two-signal reading (`safety_signal.harm_flagged === true` OR any `acts_blocked[].category === 'harm'`); confirmed canonical (founder option (a)); **no code change** (live `zone3-boundary.ts` already implements it); resolves the Stage-B Diagnostic-uncertain (symptom-level) flag under PR10. **A2** (Elevated): a microcent-precise R5 cost-health accumulator (`reflect-cost-tracker.ts` + `sage_reflect_cost_tracker` table) wired fail-soft into `route.ts` `makeMeter` after the bill persists (skipped on resume → no double-count); the integer-cents loop bill is byte-for-byte unchanged; decoupled from `increment_api_usage`/`loop_billing_events`. **A4** (Elevated): a conditional 5th Sonnet call (`extractQ5` + `Q5_SYSTEM` + `isQ5Ambiguous`) — `buildQ5Deterministic` runs first; escalation fires only when the Q5 answer is substantive AND carries a word-boundary change cue, letting the engine's FD-R2 `q5ConfirmsChange` gate be satisfied from a genuine change; documented R5 bound raised ≤4→≤5. **A1** (Elevated): two cleartext scalars (`complexity int`, `calibration_all_correct boolean`) on `sage_reflect_sessions` written at `persistCompletion`, and `getCrossSessionContext` replacing `buildContext`'s hardcoded empties on the answer path (last-3 completed rows → `PriorSessionSummary`; streak walk over `calibration_all_correct`); read fails CLOSED to empty context (never a 503).

**Reasoning:** Makes the live (gated) product faithful to its locked design — Sage Reflect was feeding the engine empty cross-session context and rounding sub-cent cost to zero; A1/A2/A4 feed real data faithfully. Built before the C rename (locked order A→C→E) so C renames finished code once. A1 open-question resolved against `engine.ts`: `PriorSessionSummary.total_failures` = distortions + assent failures + impulse patterns (the three causal-layer logs, per `countFailures`), NOT just synkatathesis. PR15 consult: no Anthropic-canonical primitive substitutes for these product-internal refinements; the load-bearing reuse is SageReasoning's own substrate (the `incrementCostTracker` microcent pattern, `usageToCents`/`sonnetCostMicrocents`, the engine's DI seam). PR16: A-track strengthens the live product (positioning neutral; dogfood relevance n/a — internal metering/extraction).

## 2026-05-23 — D-SAGE-CALLING-E1-AGENT-CARD-VERDICT-PERSIST-2026-05-23

**Decision:** Built Track E item 1 (E#1) — persist the verified Agent-Card chosen-role hint on the `discovery_sessions` row at session-open and read it on the Hard-Gate approval path, so the five-specification assembly's `role` reflects a verified card (`chosen_role`) instead of defaulting to `individual_nature`. Founder elections at open (AskUserQuestion): (1) bite = **E#1**; (2) what to store = **role-hint column** (a single nullable `agent_card_role_hint`, not a boolean and not both). AI recommendations (founder may override at close): persist **at session-open** only (folded into the existing creation INSERT — no new write, no new failure mode); **fail-open** (absent/unverified/spoofed card → NULL → today's default behaviour).

**Reasoning:** Closes the one actionable pre-launch Sage Calling follow-on surfaced in `/drafts/2026-05-23-track-followons-design-pack.md` §E: the D-13 verdict was computed and logged but discarded, so `approve/route.ts` always passed `null` into `buildDiscoveredPurpose` and the role defaulted. A verified Agent Card IS the agent's formal A2A commitment — the chosen-role persona — so persisting the hint makes the verdict carry through. Role-hint column chosen over a boolean because it is exactly the type the assembly consumes (`DiscoveredPurposeRole | null`), needs no derivation on read, and is forward-compatible if card verification later yields other personae (R18c); chosen over "both" to honour R17i (the hint is the only field the assembly needs; the verdict reason/URL/body stay observability-only). **PR15 consult:** `.claude/skills/anthropic/` (17 skills) + `/operations/agentic-commerce-findings-downstream-order.md` checked — no Anthropic-canonical primitive substitutes for persisting this product's own verdict in its own table (project-internal persistence); F1–F4 target other sessions (FPE-5, Stage 4 G3, A5, A12), none fires for Sage Calling. **PR16 lens:** positioning **neutral** (the verdict is engine-internal per R4, never surfaced; minor R0 audit-trail strengthening as the chosen-role provenance now persists); dogfood relevance **no** (internal persistence, not `/api/reason`-consultable). **Cache-drift check:** no governed surface (manifest / protocol / project-instructions / knowledge-gaps / build-arc architecture) references the changed identifiers → no cache update; `D-CACHE-DRIFT-…` not logged.

**Files touched:**
- `website/supabase-discovery-sessions-agent-card-role-hint-migration.sql` (NEW) — idempotent additive `agent_card_role_hint text` column on `discovery_sessions` + four-persona enum CHECK (passes on NULL, house-style) + VERIFY block + commented ROLLBACK (DROP CONSTRAINT + DROP COLUMN).
- `website/src/lib/sage-calling/session-store.ts` — `DiscoverySessionRow` gains `agent_card_role_hint: DiscoveredPurposeRole | null`; `initialSessionInsert` + `createSession` accept an optional hint folded into the INSERT only when present (minimised shape preserved for the no-card case); `DiscoveredPurposeRole` type imported.
- `website/src/app/api/calling/route.ts` — `fetchAndVerifyAgentCard` now returns the verdict's `role_hint` (was `void`); the hint is captured at the optional-card step and passed to `createSession` at cold-open (session-open persistence).
